body.text: I
body.translated_text: I

body.text: namo buddhāya // evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / gṛdhrakūṭe parvate 'nantaratnaśikhare dharmadhātugarbhe prāsāde mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ pañcaviṃśatibhir bhikṣusahasraiḥ / sarvair arhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravair niḥkleśair vaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair ājāneyair mahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyair apahṛtabhārair anuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramiprāptaiḥ / ājñātakauṇḍinyapramukhaiś cāṣṭaṣaṣṭibhir mahāśrāvakaiḥ, dvāsaptatibhir bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ / tadyathā mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena, dhanaśriyā ca buddhiśriyā ca bhaiṣajyarājena ca bhaiṣajyasamudgatena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / sarvair avaivartikadharmacakrapravartakaiḥ, sarvai ratnakūṭavaipulyasūtraparipṛcchākuśalaiḥ, dharmameghabhūmipratilabdhaiḥ, sumerubhūtaiḥ prajñayā, sarvaiḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānutpādājātābhāvadharmaparibhāvitaiḥ, mahāgaṃbhīradharmanirbhāsaiḥ, (

children.translated_text: JĀA 20

conducting themselves in the manner of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, dispatched by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of <s>Tathāgatas</s> from various world-systems, all born from the cultivation of supernatural powers, established in the inherent nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>. Thus have I heard: At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, at the summit of infinite jewels, in the palace called the Womb of <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality), together with a great assembly of monks — twenty-five thousand monks — all of them <s>Arhats</s> (Worthy Ones), with defilements destroyed, free from afflictions, self-mastered, with minds well-liberated, with wisdom well-liberated, thoroughbreds, great elephants, who had done what was to be done, accomplished what was to be accomplished, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, exhausted the fetters of existence, with minds well-liberated through perfect knowledge, having reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states — led by <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, sixty-eight great <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers); and seventy-two hundred thousand koṭis of niyutas of <s>bodhisattvas</s> — namely, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince, <s>Dhanaśrī</s>, <s>Buddhiśrī</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyasamudgata</s> — all turners of the irreversible wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, all skilled in the inquiries of the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> Vaipulya Sūtras, who had attained the <s>Dharmameghā-bhūmi</s> (Cloud of Dharma Stage), like <s>Sumeru</s> in wisdom, all pervaded by the <s>dharmas</s> of emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, non-arising, unborn, and non-existence, radiant with the profoundly deep <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavata etad abhūt / yan nv ahaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahājavabalavegasthāmasaṃjananārthaṃ dhārmīṃ kathāṃ kathayeyam, yad gaṅgānadīvālikāsamebhyo lokadhātubhyo mahaujaskamahaujaskān bodhisattvān mahāsattvān saṃnipāteyam / yan nv ahaṃ mahādharmanirdeśasya paridīpanāyai nimittam ādarśayeyam, mahāntam avabhāsaṃ kuryām / yan me bodhisattvā mahāsattvā āgatya mahādharmanirdeśaṃ paripṛccheyur iti /
body.translated_text: At that time, this thought arose in the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Suppose I were to teach a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of generating great speed, strength, force, and power in the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>; suppose I were to gather together the most mighty <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> from world-systems equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>; suppose I were to display a sign for the illumination of the great <s>Dharma</s> teaching and produce a great radiance, so that the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, having come, might inquire about the great <s>Dharma</s> teaching.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ daśasu dikṣv asaṃkhyeyācintyatrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamaṃ lokadhātuṃ mahāraśmimeghair avabhāsayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that moment illuminated world-systems in the ten directions, equal in number to the atoms in innumerable, inconceivable trichiliocosms, with great clouds of radiance.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena daśabhyo digbhya ekaikasmād digbhāgād daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā āgacchanti sma / (

children.translated_text: JĀA 21

children.text: ) teṣām ekaiko bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'cintyābhir bodhisattvavikurvaṇābhir āgatya bhagavato 'nurūpām acintyāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā svakasvakapraṇidhānabalanirjāteṣu padmāsaneṣu bhagavataḥ purato nyaṣīdan / bhagavantam animiṣaṃ nirīkṣamāṇā sthitā abhūvan //
children.translated_text: Each one of those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, having arrived through inconceivable <s>bodhisattva</s> transformations, having performed an inconceivable offering befitting the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down before the <s>Bhagavān</s> upon lotus seats arisen from the power of their own individual vows. They remained gazing upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> without blinking.

body.translated_text: At that time, from each of the ten directions, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of ten inexpressible hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of <s>Buddha</s>-fields came forth.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena dharmadhātugarbhe prāsādamadhye mahāratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanaṃ prādurabhūt / asaṃkhyeyayojanakoṭīvistāram, anupūrvasamucchritam, sarvaprabhāsamaṇiratnamayam, vidyutpradīpam, maṇiratnavedikāparivṛtam, acintyaprabhāsamaṇiratnadaṇḍam, anupamamaṇiratnaparivāram, anupamātikrāntaprabhāvamaṇiratnadāmakṛtaśobham, vaśirājamaṇiratnajālasaṃchannam, nānāmaṇiratnapratyuptam, samucchritacchatradhvajapatākam / tasya ca mahāmaṇiratnapadmagarbhasiṃhāsanasyopari samantād daśāsaṃkhyeyāni raśmikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma / te ca raśmayo daśasu dikṣv anyonyān lokadhātūn mahatāvabhāsena spharanti sma /
body.translated_text: At that time, in the middle of the palace called the Womb of <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, a great jeweled lotus-womb lion-throne appeared — extending for innumerable koṭis of <s>yojanas</s> in breadth, rising gradually upward, made entirely of all-radiant gem-jewels, brilliant like lightning, surrounded by gem-jewel balustrades, with inconceivable radiant gem-jewel pillars, accompanied by incomparable gem-jewel retinues, adorned with garlands of gems of unsurpassed and transcendent splendor, covered with a net of sovereign-king gem-jewels, inlaid with various gem-jewels, with raised parasols, banners, and flags. From that great gem-jewel lotus-womb lion-throne, ten innumerable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of rays issued forth in all directions. Those rays pervaded the world-systems in the ten directions with a great radiance.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena daśadiśy ekaikasmād digbhāgād daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśakrabrahmalokapālā āgacchanti sma / tatra kecid ratnakūṭāgāraniṣaṇṇāsaṃkhyeyācintyāpsaraḥkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasaṃgītisaṃpravāditair (

children.translated_text: JĀA 22

children.text: ) āgacchanti sma / kecit puṣpamayaiḥ, kecid uragasāracandanamayaiḥ, kecid muktāmayaiḥ, kecid vajramayaiḥ, kecid vajraprabhāsamaṇiratnamayaiḥ, kecij jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayaiḥ, kecit sarvaprabhāsasamuccayamaṇiratnarājamayaiḥ, kecid vaśirājamaṇiratnamayaiḥ, kecic cintāmaṇiratnamayaiḥ, kecic chakrābhilagnamaṇiratnamayaiḥ, kecit sāgarapratiṣṭhānaviśuddharatnavyūhasamantaraśmiprabhāmaṇimahāratnamayakūṭāgāraniṣaṇṇāsaṃkhyeyācintyāpsaraḥkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasaṃgītisaṃpravāditair āgacchanti sma / āgatya ca bhagavato 'cintyātulyāmāpyāṃ parimāṇābhikrāntāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā, ekānte svapraṇidhānanirjāteṣv āsaneṣu niṣīdanti sma / niṣīdya bhagavantam animiṣaṃ nirīkṣantaḥ sthitā abhūvan /
children.translated_text: some came in those made of flowers, some of finest sandalwood, some of pearls, some of diamonds, some of diamond-radiant gem-jewels, some of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, some of the king of gems combining all radiances, some of sovereign-king gem-jewels, some of wish-fulfilling gem-jewels, some of wheel-attached gem-jewels, some came seated in pinnacled mansions made of the great gem of ocean-established pure jewel-array, all-surrounding radiant gems, with innumerable, inconceivable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of celestial nymphs playing music. Having arrived and performed an inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, and surpassing offering to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, they sat down to one side upon seats arisen from their own vows. Having sat down, they remained gazing upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> without blinking.

body.translated_text: At that time, from each of the ten directions, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and world-guardians — equal in number to the atoms of ten inexpressible hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of <s>Buddha</s>-fields — came forth. Among them, some came seated in jeweled pinnacled mansions with innumerable, inconceivable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of celestial nymphs playing music;

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt / nānāmahāmaṇiratnavṛkṣair divyaiḥ puṣpavṛkṣair vastravṛkṣair uragasāracandanagandhavṛkṣair alaṃkṛtaḥ, candrasūryavidyutpradīpamaṇiratnajālasaṃcchannaḥ, ucchritacchatradhvajapatākaḥ / sarvavṛkṣāś cāsaṃkhyeyāpsaraḥkoṭīniyutaśatasahasrārdhakāyikā muktāhāraparigṛhītā mahāmaṇiratnadāmaparigṛhītāḥ sthitā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: At that time, this trichiliocosm became established as if made of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold — adorned with various great gem-jewel trees, divine flower-trees, garment-trees, and finest sandalwood fragrance trees; covered with a net of moon, sun, lightning-lamp gem-jewels; with raised parasols, banners, and flags. And all the trees stood with innumerable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of celestial nymphs appearing half-bodied, wearing pearl necklaces, adorned with great gem-jewel garlands.

body.text: II
body.translated_text: II

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena tato mahāmaṇiratnapadmagarbhāt siṃhāsanād imā gāthā niścaranti sma /
body.translated_text: At that time, from that great gem-jewel lotus-womb lion-throne, these verses issued forth:

children.text: āgaccha niṣīda narendrarājā ahaṃ hi te puṇyabalena udgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Come, sit down, O king among leaders of men — I have arisen through the power of your merit;

children.text: saṃpūrṇasaṃkalpa ahaṃ tvam adya saṃdhārayiṣye dvipadottamaṃ jinam // 1 //
children.translated_text: I am of fulfilled resolve — today I shall support you, O supreme among bipeds, O <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror).

children.text: mamātmabhāvo ratanāmayo hy ayaṃ ratnaikapadmaṃ mama madhyasaṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: This body of mine is made of jewels; a single jeweled lotus is established in my center;

children.text: manoramaṃ tubhya kṛtena nāyakāḥ saṃkalpa pūrehi mamādya tāyinaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Delightful [it is] — made for you, O Leaders; fulfill the resolve today, O Protectors, upon me.

children.text: niṣadya ratnāmayi padmi asmiṃ śobhehi māṃ sarvam imaṃ ca lokam /
children.translated_text: Having sat upon this jeweled lotus, adorn me and this entire world;

children.text: deśehi dharmaṃ bahuprāṇikoṭināṃ yaṃ śruta siṃhāsana īdṛśaṃ labhet // 3 //
children.translated_text: Teach the <s>Dharma</s> to many koṭis of living beings — having heard which, one would obtain a throne such as this.

children.text: raśmī sahasrā tava gātrasaṃbhavāḥ prabhāsayanto bahulokadhātum /
children.translated_text: Thousands of rays born from your body, illuminating many world-systems —

children.text: prāmodyajātasya hi lakṣaṇaṃ imaṃ samākramā mahya kṛtena nāyakāḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: This is a sign of joy arising; ascend upon me, O Leaders, by your deeds.

children.text: kṣipraṃ niṣīdasva kuruṣva 'nugrahaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā dhārita aṣṭakoṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Quickly sit down and bestow your grace — formerly, eighty koṭis [of Buddhas] were borne by me

children.text: asmin pradeśe munināṃ svayaṃbhuvāṃ bhagavan pīhādya karotv anugraham // 5 //
children.translated_text: In this very place, of self-arisen sages — O <s>Bhagavān</s>, may you now bestow your grace upon this [seat].

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān utthāya pūrvakād āsanāt tatra mahāratnapadmagarbhe siṃhāsane niṣadya paryaṅkaṃbaddhī sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ svavalokayati sma / sāmutkarṣikāyāś ca dharmadeśanāyās teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ nimittam akārṣīt /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rising from his former seat, sat down cross-legged upon that great jeweled lotus-womb lion-throne and surveyed the entire assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And he made a sign for the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of the highest kind to those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena sarvāvān bodhisattvagaṇa evaṃ cintayati sma / yan nv ayaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto 'nutpādānirodhaṃ tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paripṛcchet, ciraśruto 'yam asmābhir dharmaparyāya iti /
body.translated_text: At that time, the entire assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s> thought thus: 'Suppose this <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, were to question the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, about non-arising and non-cessation — for we have long heard of this <s>Dharma</s> discourse.'

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavato 'ntikān nimittaṃ viditvā teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāya bhagavantam etad avocat / anutpādo 'nirodha iti bhagavann ucyate, katamasyaitad bhagavan dharmasyādhivacanam anutpādo 'nirodha iti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, having discerned the sign from the Blessed One and having known with his mind the mental deliberations of those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, said this to the Blessed One: "Non-arising and non-ceasing" — thus it is said, Blessed One. Of which <s>dharma</s>, Blessed One, is this the designation: "non-arising and non-ceasing"?

body.text: imāś ca gāthā abhāṣat /
body.translated_text: And he spoke these verses:

body.text: anirodham anutpādaṃ bravīṣi tvaṃ vināyaka /

children.translated_text: What is the defining characteristic and etymology of that, O Greatly Wise One? // 1 //

body.translated_text: You speak of non-ceasing and non-arising, O Guide —

children.translated_text: How is this called non-ceasing and non-arising?
Explain with examples and reasons, O Great Sage. // 2 //

children.text: samāgateme bahubodhisattvā jñānārthinaḥ tvāṃ ca vibho 'bhivanditum /
children.translated_text: These many <s>bodhisattvas</s> have assembled, seekers of wisdom, to venerate you, O Mighty One,

children.text: saṃpreṣitā lokavināyakebhir deśehi saddharmam udāram uttamam // 3 //
children.translated_text: Sent by the Guides of the World — teach the noble, supreme true <s>Dharma</s>. // 3 //

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam etad avocat / sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ, sādhu khalu punas tvaṃ mañjuśrīs tathāgatam etam arthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase / bahujanahitāya tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ pratipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ caitarhy āgatānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ buddhabhūmiprāpaṇārtham / anuttrāsas te mañjuśrīr asmin sthāne yogaḥ karaṇīyo na (

children.translated_text: JĀA 26

children.text: ) bhayaṃ na stambhitatvam / jñānapratisaraṇena ca te mañjuśrīr bhavitavyam / tathāgatasyaitam arthaṃ nirdeśataḥ / anutpādo 'nirodha iti mañjuśrīs tathāgatasyaitad adhivacanam / tadyathā mañjuśrīr iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī mahāvaiḍūryamayī saṃsthitā bhavet / evaṃ ca saṃsthitā bhaved yathā tasyāṃ vaiḍūryamayāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ trayastriṃśadbhavanasya, śakrasya devānām indrasya, vaijayantasya ca prāsādasya pratibhāsaḥ saṃdṛśyet / śakraś ca devānām indras tatra divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ paricārayan saṃdṛśyet /
children.translated_text: fear, no paralysis. And you, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, must rely on wisdom. The <s>Tathāgata</s> will explain this matter. 'Non-arising and non-ceasing' — <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, this is the designation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Suppose, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, this great earth were established as made of great <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli). And suppose it were so established that in that <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-made great earth, the reflection of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and of the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace would be seen. And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, would be seen there sporting, delighting, and enjoying himself with the five divine strands of sense-pleasure.

body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince: "Well done, well done, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that you think to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> about this matter. You, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, have set forth for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake of the great multitude, for their benefit, welfare, and happiness — of gods and humans — and for the purpose of leading the <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who have come here to the stage of <s>Buddhahood</s>. You should be without fear, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>; in this matter, effort should be made — no

body.text: atha tasmin samaye devāḥ sarvajambūdvīpakāḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāḥ saṃcodayeyuḥ / āgacchatha bho naranāryaḥ / paśyatemaṃ śakraṃ devānām indraṃ vaijayante prāsāde divyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ krīḍantaṃ ramantaṃ paricārayantam / āgacchatha bho naranārigaṇāḥ / dānāni dadata puṇyāni kuruta / śīlaṃ ca samādāya vartayata / īdṛśeṣu vaijayanteṣu prāsādeṣu krīḍiṣyatha ramiṣyatha paricārayiṣyatha śakratvāni ca kariṣyatha / īdṛśyā ca riddhyā samanvāgatā bhaviṣyatha / yādṛśyā ca śakro devānām indro divyaiḥ paribhogaiḥ samarpitaḥ samanvaṅgībhūta iti /
body.translated_text: Then at that time, all the gods and the men and women, boys and girls of all <s>Jambudvīpa</s> would be exhorted: 'Come, good men and women! Behold this <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, sporting, delighting, and enjoying himself in the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace with the five divine strands of sense-pleasure! Come, good assemblies of men and women! Give gifts, perform meritorious deeds, and undertake the precepts! In such <s>Vaijayanta</s> palaces you will sport, delight, and enjoy yourselves, and you will become <s>Śakras</s>! And you will be endowed with such supernatural power as <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, is furnished and endowed with divine enjoyments!'

body.text: atha mañjuśrīs te strīpuruṣadārakadārikās tasyāṃ vaiḍūryamayāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ trayastriṃśadbhavanasya, vaijayantasya prāsādasya, śakrasya devānām indrasya pratibhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvāñjalipragṛhaṃ kuryuḥ / puṣpāṇi ca kṣiperan (

children.translated_text: JĀA 27

children.text: ) gandhāṃś ca kṣiperann evaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣante / vayam apy evaṃrūpā bhavema yādṛśaḥ śakro devānām indraḥ, vayam apy evaṃ vaijayante prāsāde krīḍema ramema parivārayema yathāyaṃ śakro devānām indra iti /
children.translated_text: and they would scatter incense, speaking thus: 'May we also become of such a form as <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods! May we also sport, delight, and be attended in the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace just as this <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods!'

body.translated_text: Then, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, those men and women, boys and girls, having seen the reflection of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, in that <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-made great earth, would make <s>añjali</s> (joined palms). And they would scatter flowers,

body.text: na ca te sattvā evaṃ saṃjānanti sma / pratibhāso 'yaṃ vaiḍūryamayāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ yatra trayastriṃśadbhavanam, vaijayantaś ca prāsādaḥ, śakraś ca devānām indraḥ pariśuddhatvād mahāvaiḍūryasya pratibhāsaḥ saṃdṛśyata iti / te śakratvam abhinandanto dānāni ca dadati, puṇyāni ca kurvanti, śīlaṃ ca samādāya vartante / tatra ca trayastriṃśadbhavane pratibhāsa upapattaye kuśalamūlāni ca pariṇāmayanti /
body.translated_text: But those beings did not realize: 'This is a reflection in the <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-made great earth — the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods — the reflection is seen due to the purity of the great <s>vaiḍūrya</s>.' Delighting in [the prospect of] becoming <s>Śakra</s>, they give gifts, perform meritorious deeds, and undertake the precepts. And they dedicate roots of merit for rebirth in that <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven of the reflection.

body.text: yathā mañjuśrīḥ tatra ca vaiḍūryamayāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ nāsti tatra trayastriṃśadbhavanam, na vaijayantaś ca prāsādaḥ, na ca śakro devānām indraḥ / api tu pariśuddhatvād mahāvaiḍūryasya saṃdṛśyate trayastriṃśadbhavanam, vaijayantaś ca prāsādaḥ, śakrasya devānām indraḥ / sa cāsan notpanno na niruddhaḥ pariśuddhatvād mahāvaiḍūryasya pratibhāsaḥ saṃdṛśyate /
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in that <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-made great earth there is no <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, no <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, and no <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods — yet due to the purity of the great <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, are seen. And that [reflection] was not arisen, not ceased — the reflection is seen due to the purity of the great <s>vaiḍūrya</s>.

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīḥ pariśuddhatvāc cittasya subhāvitatvād bhāvanāyāḥ sattvānāṃ tathāgatātmabhāvadarśanaṃ bhavati / tathāgatānubhāvena mañjuśrīḥ sattvās tathāgataṃ paśyanti / sa cābhūto 'nutpanno 'niruddho na bhāvo nābhāvo na dṛśyo nādṛśyo na lokyo nālokyo na caityo nācaityo na san nāsan /
body.translated_text: Just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, through the purity of mind and the thorough cultivation of meditation, beings have the vision of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> form. Through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, beings see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Yet he is unreal, unarisen, unceased — neither being nor non-being, neither seen nor unseen, neither worldly nor beyond the world, neither a memorial nor not a memorial, neither existent nor non-existent.

body.text: atha ca mañjuśrīḥ sattvās tathāgatapratibhāsam ārambaṇīkṛtvā puṣpāṇi kṣipanti, gandhān vastrāṇi ratnāni ca kṣipanti / evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣante / vayam apy evaṃrūpā bhavema yādṛśas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti / te buddhajñānābhilāṣiṇo dānāni ca dadati, puṇyāni ca kurvanti, śīlaṃ ca samādāya vartante / tac ca kuśalamūlaṃ tathāgatajñānapratilambhāya (

children.translated_text: JĀA 28

children.text: ) pariṇāmayanti / tadyathā mañjuśrīs tatra mahāvaiḍūryamayāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ śakrasya devānām indrasya pratibhāso neñjati, na manyate, na prapañcayati, na kalpayati, na vikalpayati / akalpo 'vikalpo 'cintyo 'manasikāraḥ śāntaḥ śītībhūto 'nutpādo 'nirodho 'dṛṣṭo 'śruto 'nāghrāto 'nāsvādito 'spṛṣṭo 'nimitto 'vijñaptiko 'vijñāpanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, on that great <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-made great earth, the reflection of <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, does not move, does not think, does not proliferate, does not construct, does not discriminate — it is unconstructed, undiscriminated, inconceivable, without mental engagement, peaceful, cooled, unarisen, unceased, unseen, unheard, unsmelled, untasted, untouched, signless, without information, not to be communicated.

body.translated_text: And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, beings, having made the reflection of the <s>Tathāgata</s> their support, scatter flowers, scatter incense, garments, and jewels. And they speak thus: 'May we also become of such a form as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One!' Desiring the wisdom of the <s>Buddha</s>, they give gifts, perform meritorious deeds, and undertake the precepts. And they dedicate those roots of merit for attaining the wisdom of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddho neñjati, na manyate, na prapañcayati, na kalpayati, na vikalpayati / akalpo 'vikalpo 'cintyo 'manasikāraḥ śāntaḥ śītībhūto 'nutpādo 'nirodho 'dṛṣṭo 'śruto 'nāghrāto 'nāsvādito 'spṛṣṭo 'nimitto 'vijñaptiko 'vijñāpanīyaḥ / anutpādagatiko hi mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ / atha ca pratibimba iva lokeṣu dṛśyate / yathādhimuktikānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ darśanavaimātratayā, āyuḥpramāṇavaimātratāṃ darśayati / paripācanādhimuktibalādhānatayā bodhibhājaneṣu sattveṣu pratibhāsaprāpto bhavati / yathāśayādhimuktyā ca sattvā dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti / yathāśayena triyānam iti saṃjānanti, yathāśayena cādhimucyante //
body.translated_text: Just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, does not move, does not think, does not proliferate, does not construct, does not discriminate — he is unconstructed, undiscriminated, inconceivable, without mental engagement, peaceful, cooled, unarisen, unceased, unseen, unheard, unsmelled, untasted, untouched, signless, without information, not to be communicated. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, has gone to non-arising. And yet he appears in the worlds like a reflection. According to the dispositions of beings who have resolved [upon awakening], he displays a diversity of appearances and a diversity of life-spans. Through the power of his resolve to ripen [beings], he comes to appear as a reflection among beings who are vessels of awakening. And according to their dispositions and aspirations, beings hear the <s>Dharma</s>. According to their dispositions they perceive three vehicles, and according to their dispositions they are resolved.

body.text: tadyathā mañjuśrīr devānāṃ trayastriṃśānāṃ puṇyabalapariniṣpannānāṃ dharmaśabdānāṃ mahādharmadundubhir upari vaijayantasya prasādasyāntarīkṣagatā cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntā, adṛśyā, anālokyā sarvadevaputraiḥ /
body.translated_text: Suppose, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the Great <s>Dharma</s>-drum, which is accomplished by the power of their merit and through which they hear the <s>Dharma</s>-sounds, is stationed in the sky above the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace — beyond the range of vision, invisible, unable to be perceived by all the sons of the gods.

body.text: atha ca punar mañjuśrīḥ sā mahādharmadundubhiḥ / yasmin (

children.translated_text: JĀA 29

children.text: ) samaye devās trayastriṃśatkāyikā tīvrasatatasamitaṃ divyaiḥ kāmakrīḍāratiparibhogaiḥ pramattā bhavanti, na bhūyaḥ sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāṃ praviśya dharmaṃ saṃgāyanti, śakraś ca yadā devānām indro divyaiḥ kāmakrīḍaratiparibhogaiḥ pramatto bhavati, na dharmāsane niṣadya dharmaṃ bhāṣate /
children.translated_text: time when the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods become intoxicated with intense, continuous, and unceasing divine sense-pleasures, sports, and enjoyments, and no longer enter the <s>Sudharmā</s> divine assembly hall to chant the <s>Dharma</s>, and when <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, being intoxicated with divine sense-pleasures, sports, and enjoyments, does not sit on the <s>Dharma</s>-seat to teach the <s>Dharma</s> —

body.translated_text: And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that Great <s>Dharma</s>-drum — at the

body.text: tasmin samaye mañjuśrīḥ sā mahādharmadundubhir adṛṣyā cānālokyā cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntāntarīkṣagatā tādṛśaṃ dharmaśabdaṃ niścārayati / yena ca dharmaśabdena sarvān trayastriṃśatkāyikān devān svareṇa vijñapayati / anityā mārṣā rūpaśabdagandharasasparśā mā pramattacāriṇo bhavatha / mā kṣipram asmād bhavanāc cyaviṣyatha / duḥkhā mārṣāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, anātmano mārṣāḥ sarvasaṃskārāḥ, śūnyā mārṣāḥ sarvasaṃskārā mā pramādam āpadyatha / duḥkham itaś cyavitānāṃ punar atropapattir bhaviṣyati / saṃgāyata mārṣā dharmam, dharmārāmaratiratā bhavatha dharmasārāḥ, dharmanimnāḥ, dharmapravaṇāḥ, dharmānusmṛtimanasikārāḥ / mārṣā viharatha yūyaṃ punar ebhir evaṃ divyaiḥ kāmakrīḍāratiparibhogaiḥ, avirahitā bhaviṣyatheti /
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that great <s>Dharma</s>-drum, invisible and imperceptible, having passed beyond the range of sight, situated in the sky, emits such a <s>Dharma</s>-sound. And by that <s>Dharma</s>-sound it makes known to all the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods with its voice: 'Impermanent, O sirs, are forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches! Do not conduct yourselves heedlessly! Do not quickly [fall] from this state...'

body.text: tena khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ samayena tasyā adṛśyā arūpiṇyā akalpyāyā avikalpāyāś cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntāyā anutpannāniruddhāyā vākpathasamatikrāntāyāś cittamanovijñānāpagatāyā mahādharmadundubheḥ śabdena sarve trayastriṃśatkāyikā devāḥ saṃcoditā bhītās trastā udvignodvignāḥ (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 30]

children.text: ) sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāṃ praviśya dharmārāmaratiratā viharanti / dharmasārāḥ, dharmanimnāḥ, dharmapravaṇāḥ, dharmānusmṛtimanasikārā bhavanti / te tataś cyutā viśeṣagāmino bhavanti / śakraś ca devānām indras tasmin samaye sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāṃ praviśya dharmāsane niṣadya dharmaṃ deśayati /
children.translated_text: and they enter the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall of the gods, where they dwell delighting in the pleasure-garden of the <s>Dharma</s>. They become those whose essence is the <s>Dharma</s>, inclined toward the <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, with minds given to the recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>. Having fallen from there, they become those who go to higher destinies. And <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, at that time enters the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall, sits upon the <s>Dharma</s>-seat, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Then again, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, at that time, by the sound of that great <s>Dharma</s>-drum — which is invisible, formless, inconceivable, beyond conceptualization, having passed beyond the range of sight, unborn and unceasing, having passed beyond the path of speech, devoid of mind, thought, and consciousness — all the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods are stirred, frightened, alarmed, and deeply agitated,

body.text: yadā ca mañjuśrīr asurā devaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmayanti / tatra yadā trayastriṃśā devāḥ parābhavaṃ gacchanti / tadā sā dharmadundubhī tādṛśaśabdaṃ niścārayati / yena śabdenāsurā bhītās trastā udvignodvignāḥ palāyanti /
body.translated_text: And when, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Asuras</s> wage war with the gods, and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods meet with defeat, then that <s>Dharma</s>-drum emits such a sound by which the <s>Asuras</s>, frightened, alarmed, and deeply agitated, flee.

body.text: na ca mañjuśrīs tasyā mahādharmadundubheḥ kaścit saṃpādayitā vātmabhāvo vā saṃvidyate / adṛśyā mañjuśrīḥ sā mahādharmadundubhir anālokyāsatyābhūtācittācetanānimittārūpiṇyarutānātmabhāvādvayā cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntā /
body.translated_text: Yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there is no one who produces that great <s>Dharma</s>-drum, nor is any self-nature to be found in it. That great <s>Dharma</s>-drum, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is invisible, imperceptible, untrue, non-existent, without mind, without consciousness, without cause, formless, without sound, without self-nature, non-dual, having passed beyond the range of sight.

body.text: atha ca mañjuśrīs trayastriṃśatkāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ pūrvaparikarmakṛtānāṃ mahādharmadundubheḥ śabdo niścarati / trāyastriṃśānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sarvopadravopāyāsopakleśopaśāntaye saṃvartate /
body.translated_text: And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for those sons of gods among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> who have performed prior preparatory practices, the sound of the great <s>Dharma</s>-drum goes forth. It serves for the pacification of all calamities, afflictions, and defilements of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> sons of gods.

body.text: yathā mañjuśrīs tasyā mahādundubher adṛśyo 'nātmabhāvo 'nālokyo 'sann abhūto 'cinto 'cetano 'nimitto (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 31]

children.text: ) 'rūpy aruto 'bhāvo 'dvayaś cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntaḥ, pūrvakarmavipākena trayastriṃśatkāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sarvopadravopāyāsopakleśopaśāntaye śabdo niścarati / pramattāṃś ca devaputrān dharmaśabdena saṃcodayati / sa ca dharmaśabdas trayastriṃśatkāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ sarvopadravopāyāsopakleśopaśāntaye saṃvartate /
children.translated_text: formless, without sound, without substantial existence, non-dual, having passed beyond the range of sight — yet by the ripening of prior <s>karma</s>, a sound goes forth for the pacification of all calamities, afflictions, and defilements of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> sons of gods. It rouses the heedless sons of gods with the <s>Dharma</s>-sound. And that <s>Dharma</s>-sound serves for the pacification of all calamities, afflictions, and defilements of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> sons of gods.

body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the self-nature of that great drum is invisible, imperceptible, non-existent, unreal, inconceivable, without consciousness, without cause,

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'dṛśyo 'nālokyo 'nātmabhāvo 'sann abhūto 'citto 'cetano 'nimitto 'rūpy aruto 'dvayo 'bhāvaś cakṣuḥpathasamatikrāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: In exactly the same way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, is invisible, imperceptible, without self-nature, non-existent, unreal, without mind, without consciousness, without cause, formless, without sound, non-dual, without substantial existence, having passed beyond the range of sight.

body.text: atha ca mañjuśrīḥ sattvāḥ pūrvakarmavipākena yathāśayādhimuktyā dharmaśabdaṃ niścarantaṃ saṃjānanti / sa ca dharmaśabdaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvopadravopāyāsopakleśopaśāntaye saṃvartate / dharmasvaranirghoṣeṇa tathāgataghoṣasvara iti loke saṃkhyāṃ gacchati /
body.translated_text: And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, beings, through the ripening of their prior <s>karma</s>, according to their dispositions and aspirations, perceive the <s>Dharma</s>-sound going forth. And that <s>Dharma</s>-sound serves for the pacification of all calamities, afflictions, and defilements of all beings. Through the utterance of the <s>Dharma</s>-voice, he becomes known in the world as '<s>Tathāgata</s>-voice.'

body.text: nāsti ca mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ, atha ca dharmasvaraghoṣeṇa tathāgata iti prajñaptir loke saṃbhavati / sattvānām eva pūrvakuśalakarmavipākena tathāgataśabdaṃ niścarantaṃ sattvāḥ saṃjānanti / sarvasattvānāṃ sarvasukhajananārthaṃ pramattānāṃ ca saṃcodanārthaṃ śabdo niścarati / te mañjuśrīḥ sattvāḥ śabdaṃ śrutvā tathāgataṃ saṃkalpayanti / ayaṃ tathāgatasyātmabhāva iti /
body.translated_text: There is no <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and yet through the utterance of the <s>Dharma</s>-voice, the designation '<s>Tathāgata</s>' arises in the world. It is only through the ripening of beings' prior wholesome <s>karma</s> that beings perceive the <s>Tathāgata</s>-sound going forth. The sound goes forth for the purpose of generating all happiness for all beings and for rousing the heedless. Those beings, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, [hearing] the sound...

body.text: ādikarmikāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ sarvabālapṛthagjanānāṃ ca tathāgatārambaṇakuśalamūlasaṃjananārthaṃ tathāgatavāk śrūyate / api tv anutpanno 'niruddho mañjuśrīs tathāgato veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are beginners, and for all ordinary foolish persons, the voice of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is heard for the purpose of generating wholesome roots that take the <s>Tathāgata</s> as their support. And for those beings who have planted wholesome roots with the intention of attaining the knowledge of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and who have the conditions for being shown the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. However, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be understood as unborn and unceased.
§8 [Manuscript and edition references: Ms. 7b2-8b4, P. 308b2-309b6, D. 282a4-283a5, T. 357 241b21-242a2, T. 358, T. 359(D) 256a18-b21.]

body.text: tadyathā mañjuśrīr nidāghakālāvasāne varṣāṇāṃ prathame māsy āgate sattvānāṃ pūrvakarmavipākena pṛthivīgatānāṃ bījagrāmabhūtagrāmasya sarvatṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatīnāṃ saṃjananārtham upari vaihāyasy āntarīkṣa ākāśe tādṛśā vāyavo vānti / yenodakaṃ saṃbhavati / saṃbhūtaṃ ca mahāpṛthivyāṃ prapatati / tena ca sarvī mahāpṛthivī saṃtarpitā bhavati / sarve jambūdvīpakāś ca sattvās tasmin samaye pramuditā bhavanti / saumanasyajātās tasya megha iti / saṃjñā loke saṃbhavati /
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, at the end of the hot season, when the first month of the rains has arrived, through the ripening of beings' prior <s>karma</s>, such winds blow above in the sky, in the atmosphere, for the purpose of generating all grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees — all the seed-communities and plant-communities situated on the earth. By those [winds], water is produced; and having been produced, it falls upon the great earth.

body.text: yasmin khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ samaya upary antarīkṣād mahān udakaskandho na nipatati, tasmin samaye sarvajambūdvīpakāḥ sattvā evaṃ cintayanti / nātra meghaḥ saṃbhavati / yadā tu mañjuśrīr upary antarīkṣād mahān vāriskandho mahāpṛthivyāṃ nipatati, sattvā evaṃ vadanti / aho mahāmegho vāri pramuñcati saṃtarpayati mahāpṛthivīm iti / na punar atra mañjuśrīr megho vā meghaprajñaptir vā vidyate / vātasaṃjanito mañjuśrīr upary antarīkṣād mahān udakaskandho nipatati / so 'pskandho mañjuśrīs tatraivāntarīkṣe 'ntardhīyate / sattvānāṃ pūrvakarmavipākena /
body.translated_text: At a time, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when a great mass of water does not fall from the sky above, at that time all beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> think: 'No cloud is forming here.' But when, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a great mass of rain falls from the sky above upon the great earth, beings say: 'Ah! A great cloud is releasing rain!'

body.text: yathā mañjuśrīs tasya vāriskandhasyopary antarīkṣe vātasaṃkṣobheṇa saṃvāryamāṇasya muñcato vāri megha iti prajñaptir bhavati / sattvānāṃ pūrvakarmavipākena / na punar atra mañjuśrīr meghaḥ saṃvidyate, na meghaprajñaptiḥ / (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 33]
The cloud, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is unborn and unceased, inaccessible to the movement of thought, freed from coming and going.

body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when that mass of rain is gathered above in the sky by the agitation of the wind and releases rain, the designation 'cloud' arises — through the ripening of beings' prior <s>karma</s>. But, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there is no cloud to be found here, nor is there a designation 'cloud.'

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīḥ pūrvakuśalamūlasaṃbhāropacitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ cānyeṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhajñānābhiprāyāṇām avaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ nirvāṇamārgasaṃdarśanahetukānām āsaṃgapratibhānas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpanna iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / sa yad bhāṣate tat sarvaṃ tathāvitathānanyathā, tasya devamanuṣyeṣu tathāgata iti nāma kṛtam / atha ca mañjuśrīḥ śabdo niścarati devamanuṣyeṣu yaduta tathāgata iti / na punar mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ saṃvidyate / animitto mañjuśrīs tathāgato nimittāpagato na deśastho na videśasthaḥ, abhūto 'nutpanno 'niruddhaḥ / tat khalu punar mañjuśrīs tathāgatapratibhāsaḥ sadevakaṃ lokaṃ dharmeṇa saṃtarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā, ādikarmikāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ cānyeṣāṃ ca sarvabālapṛthagjanānāṃ nirvāṇavainayikānāṃ pūrvakarmavipākenādarśanābhāso bhavati / teṣām evaṃ bhavati / parinirvṛtas tathāgata iti / na mañjuśrīs tathāgata utpadyate vā nirudhyate vā /
body.translated_text: In exactly the same way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, for those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who have accumulated a store of prior wholesome roots, and for other beings who have planted wholesome roots with aspirations toward the knowledge of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and for beings who have the conditions for being shown the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, of unimpeded eloquence, becomes known as 'arisen in the world.' He who...

body.text: anutpanno 'niruddho mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ / ādiparinirvṛto mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / yathā mañjuśrīr (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 34]

children.text: ) udakārambaṇenābhūtasya meghasyānutpannāniruddhasyāsato meghaprajñaptiḥ sthitā loke megha iti / evam eva mañjuśrīr dharmadeśanārambaṇenābhūtasya tathāgatasyānutpannāniruddhasyāsata ādita evājātasya nāmaprajñaptiḥ sthitā loke tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti //
children.translated_text: By means of water as a basis, the designation 'cloud' is established in the world for a cloud that is unoriginated, unborn, unceased, and non-existent — 'cloud.' In the same way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, by means of the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching as a basis, the designation by name is established in the world for the <s>Tathāgata</s> who is unoriginated, unborn, unceased, non-existent, and unborn from the very beginning — '<s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>).'

body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is unborn and unceased. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is primordially in <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>...

body.text: tadyathāpi mañjuśrīr mahābrahmānabhibhūr daśatrisāhasramahāsāhasravaśavartī divase divase sarvadevanikāyān vyavalokayati, yāvac cāturmahārājikadevanikāyaparyantān / tena khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ samayena tasya mahābrahmaṇo daśatrisāhasramahāsāhasravaśavartinaḥ sarvadevanikāyān vyavalokayataḥ, sarvadevanikāyeṣu sarvadevaputrāḥ svakasvakān kāmakrīḍāratiparibhogāṃs tyaktvā sarvatūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgītiṃ śamayitvā, kāmakrīḍāratimanasikārotsṛṣṭāḥ sagauravā añjaliṃ pragṛhya mahābrahmāṇam animiṣaṃ vyavalokayanti / sa ca mahābrahmā sarvadevanikāyeṣu muhūrtaṃ darśanaṃ dadāti / te ca devaputrās tasmin samaye mahābrahmalokopapattim ākāṅkṣanti, mahābrahmalokopapattaye ca kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayanti /
body.translated_text: For example, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the unconquered, the sovereign of the ten-fold trichiliocosm, day after day surveys all the assemblies of gods, down to the assembly of the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven. At that time, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when that <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the sovereign of the ten-fold trichiliocosm, surveys all the assemblies of gods, all the <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) in all the divine assemblies abandon their respective sensual pleasures and enjoyments, quiet all their musical instruments, drums, dances, and songs, release their minds from attention to sensual pleasures, and with reverence, joining their palms together, gaze unblinkingly at <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. And that <s>Mahābrahmā</s> grants a moment's audience in all the divine assemblies. And those <s>devaputras</s> at that time aspire to rebirth in the world of <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, and they dedicate their roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) toward rebirth in the world of <s>Mahābrahmā</s>.

body.text: sa ca mañjuśrīr mahābrahmācyavamānas tato brahmavimānād anyam adhitiṣṭhati mahābrahmāṇaṃ daśatrisāhasramahāsāhasravaśavartinaṃ pūrvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena teṣāṃ ca devaputrāṇāṃ pūrvakuśalamūlopacayena /
body.translated_text: And, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as that <s>Mahābrahmā</s> passes away from that <s>Brahmā</s>-palace, he establishes another <s>Mahābrahmā</s> as sovereign of the ten-fold trichiliocosm, by the power of his former vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) and by the accumulation of previous roots of merit of those <s>devaputras</s>.

body.text: sa ca mañjuśrīr nirmito mahābrahmā divase divase sarvadevanikāyān vyavalokayati, yāvac cāturmahārājakāyikadevanikāyān / tena khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ samayena sarveṣu devanikāyeṣu sarvadevaputrāḥ svakasvakān kāmakrīḍāratiparibhogāṃs tyaktvā sarvatūryatāḍāvacarasaṃgītiṃ praśamayitvā, kāmakrīḍāratimanasikārotsṛṣṭāḥ sagauravā añjaliṃ pragṛhya mahābrahmāṇam animiṣaṃ vyavalokayanti sma / sa ca mahābrahmā sarvadevanikāyeṣu muhūrtaṃ darśanaṃ dadāti, na ca sthānāc calati / te ca devaputrās tasmin samaye mahābrahmalokopapattim ākāṅkṣanti, brahmalokopapattaye ca kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayanti /
body.translated_text: And, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that magically created <s>Mahābrahmā</s> day after day surveys all the assemblies of gods, down to the assemblies of the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven. At that time, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all the <s>devaputras</s> in all the divine assemblies abandon their respective sensual pleasures and enjoyments, quiet all their musical instruments, drums, dances, and songs, release their minds from attention to sensual pleasures, and with reverence, joining their palms together, gaze unblinkingly at <s>Mahābrahmā</s>. And that <s>Mahābrahmā</s> grants a moment's audience in all the divine assemblies, yet does not move from his place. And those <s>devaputras</s> at that time aspire to rebirth in the world of <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, and they dedicate their roots of merit toward rebirth in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: na cātra mañjuśrīr brahmā saṃvidyate / śūnyo 'yaṃ mañjuśrīr brahmā vaśiko 'bhūto 'nakṣaro 'ghoṣo 'deśo 'bhāvo 'cintyo 'nimittaś cittamanovijñānāpagato 'nutpanno 'niruddhaḥ / atha ca mañjuśrīḥ sarvadevanikāyeṣu darśanābhāso bhavati, tasyaiva mahābrahmaṇaḥ pūrvakuśalamūlapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena teṣāṃ ca devaputrāṇāṃ pūrvakuśalamūlopacayena / na ca mañjuśrīs teṣāṃ devaputrāṇām evaṃ bhavati / nirmito 'yaṃ brahmā, śūnyo vaśiko 'bhūto 'nakṣaro 'ghoṣo 'deśo 'bhāvo 'cintyo 'nimittaś cittamanovijñānāpagato 'nutpanno 'niruddho veti /
body.translated_text: Yet in this case, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, no <s>Brahmā</s> actually exists. This <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is empty (<s>śūnya</s>), controlled, unoriginated, without syllable, without sound, without location, without existence, inconceivable, without sign, devoid of mind (<s>citta</s>), thought (<s>manas</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), unborn and unceased. And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the appearance of his vision occurs in all the divine assemblies — by the power of that very <s>Mahābrahmā's</s> former roots of merit and vow, and by the accumulation of previous roots of merit of those <s>devaputras</s>. And, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, it does not occur to those <s>devaputras</s> thus: 'This <s>Brahmā</s> is magically created, empty, controlled, unoriginated, without syllable, without sound, without location, without existence, inconceivable, without sign, devoid of mind, thought, and consciousness, unborn and unceased.'

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'py arhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ śūnyo vaśiko 'bhūto 'nakṣaro 'ghoṣo 'deśo 'bhāvo 'cintyo 'nimittaś cittamanovijñānāpagato 'nutpanno 'niruddhaḥ / atha ca punar mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvabodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānena, (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 36]

children.text: ) ādikarmiṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ ca sarvabālapṛthagjanānāṃ sarvakuśalamūlādhiṣṭhānena lakṣaṇaśatasahasrālaṃkṛtas tathāgataḥ pratibimbam iva loke saṃdṛśyate, na ca sthānāc calati /
children.translated_text: and by the power of the roots of merit of beginning <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all those who have set out in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, and all ordinary, childish beings — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, adorned with a hundred thousand marks, appears in the world like a reflection, yet does not move from his place.

body.translated_text: In the same way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, is also empty, controlled, unoriginated, without syllable, without sound, without location, without existence, inconceivable, without sign, devoid of mind, thought, and consciousness, unborn and unceased. And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, by the power of his former <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practice and vow,

body.text: na ca mañjuśrīr ādikarmikāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikānāṃ sarvabālapṛthagjanānāṃ caivaṃ bhavati / śūnyas tathāgato vaśiko 'bhūto 'nakṣaro 'ghoṣo 'deśo 'bhāvo 'cintyo 'nimittaś cittamanovijñānāpagato 'nutpanno 'niruddho ceti / atha ca mañjuśrīs tathāgatātmabhāvāl lakṣaṇaśatasahasrālaṃkṛtāt sarvatathāgateryāpatheṣu śūnyeṣu nānāvidhivicitrāṇāṃ nānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ mahādharmadeśanā niścarati / sā ca dharmadeśanā sarvasattvānāṃ sarvopadravopāyāsopakleśopaśāntaye saṃvartate / tatra ca tathāgataḥ samayaḥ sarvatropekṣako nirvikalpo nirviśeṣaḥ / tad anenāpi te mañjuśrīḥ paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam, anutpādo 'nirodha iti tathāgatasyaitad adhivacanam iti //
body.translated_text: And, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, it does not occur to beginning <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, or ordinary childish beings thus: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is empty, controlled, unoriginated, without syllable, without sound, without location, without existence, inconceivable, without sign, devoid of mind, thought, and consciousness, unborn and unceased.' Yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, from the <s>Tathāgata's</s> body, adorned with a hundred thousand marks, in all the conduct of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, which is empty, a great <s>Dharma</s>-teaching issues forth, varied and diverse, for beings of various dispositions. And that <s>Dharma</s>-teaching serves for the pacification of all afflictions, troubles, and defilements of all beings. And therein the <s>Tathāgata</s> at all times is equanimous, free from conceptual construction, without distinction. By this analogy too, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, it should be understood: 'Non-arising, non-ceasing' — this is a designation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyām ime gāthe abhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then at that time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses:

children.text: anutpādadharmaḥ satataṃ tathāgataḥ sarve ca dharmāḥ sugatena sādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is of the nature of non-arising at all times, and all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are similar to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One);

children.text: nimittagrāheṇa tu bālabuddhayo asatsu dharmeṣu caranti loke // 1 //
children.translated_text: But those of childish understanding, grasping at signs, pursue non-existent phenomena in the world. // 1 //

children.text: tathāgato hi pratibimbabhūtaḥ kuśalasya dharmasya anāsravasya /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Tathāgata</s> is like a reflection of wholesome <s>dharma</s>, free from outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>);

children.text: na cātra tathatā na tathāgato 'sti bimbaṃ ca saṃdṛśyati sarvaloke // 2 //
children.translated_text: Yet neither <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness) nor the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists herein — and yet the image is seen in the entire world. // 2 //

body.text: tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ sūryaraśmayo jambūdvīpe pūrvataram eva tāvad mahāśailendrarājānam avabhāsayanti / tataḥ paścāc cakravāḍān mahācakravāḍān avabhāsayanti / tataḥ paścād uccoccān pṛthivīpradeśān avabhāsayanti / tataḥ paścād iha jambūdvīpe nimnān pṛthivīpradeśān avabhāsayanti / te ca mañjuśrīḥ sūryaraśmayo na kalpayanti, na vikalpayanti, na cintayanti, na vicintayanti / cittamanovijñānāpagatā mañjuśrīḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ, anutpannā aniruddhāḥ, alakṣaṇā lakṣaṇāpagatāḥ, amanaskārā manaskārāpagatāḥ, aprapañcāḥ prapañcāpagatāḥ, (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 38]

children.text: ) aparidāhā niṣparidāhāḥ, naurasthā na parasthāḥ, noccā na nīcāḥ, na baddhā na muktāḥ, na jñānavanto nājñānavantaḥ, na saṃkleśā na niḥkleśāḥ, na satyavādino na mṛṣāvādinaḥ, na tīre na nimne, na sthale naughe, na tarkāvacarā nātarkāvacarāḥ, na rūpiṇo nārūpiṇaḥ / atha ca punar mañjuśrīḥ pṛthivyām uccanīcamadhyaviśeṣeṇa hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭāvabhāsasya cchāyā vaicitryaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: without burning, free from burning, neither here nor there, neither high nor low, neither bound nor liberated, neither possessing knowledge nor lacking knowledge, neither defiled nor purified, neither speaking truth nor speaking falsehood, neither on the bank nor in the depths, neither on dry land nor in a flood, neither within the range of reasoning nor beyond the range of reasoning, neither with form nor formless. And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there arises a diversity of shadow on the earth according to the distinction of high, low, and middle — of inferior, middling, and superior illumination.

body.translated_text: For example, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the rays of the sun first illuminate the great king of mountains, <s>Śailendra</s> (Sumeru), in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Then afterward they illuminate the <s>Cakravāḍa</s> and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> mountains. Then afterward they illuminate the high places of the earth. Then afterward they illuminate the low-lying places of the earth here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. And those rays of the sun, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do not construct, do not conceptualize, do not think, do not deliberate. The rays of the sun, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, are devoid of mind, thought, and consciousness — unborn, unceased, without marks, free from marks, without mental activity, free from mental activity, without conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), free from conceptual proliferation,

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'py arhan samyaksaṃbuddho na kalpayati, na vikalpayati, na cintayati, na vicintayati / cittamanovijñānāpagato mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ, anutpanno 'niruddhaḥ, alakṣaṇo lakṣaṇāpagataḥ, amanaskāro manaskārāpagataḥ, aprapañcaḥ prapañcāpagataḥ, aparidāho niṣparidāhaḥ / naurastho na pārasthaḥ, nocco na nīcaḥ, na baddho na muktaḥ, na jñānavān nājñānavān, na saṃkleśo na niḥkleśaḥ, na satyavādī na mṛṣāvādī, nāvāre na pāre, na tīre nātīre, na nimne nānimne, na sthale nāsthale, naughe nānoghe, na sarvajño nāsarvajñaḥ, na tarko nātarkaḥ, na pracāro (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 39]

children.text: ) nāpracāraḥ, na samudācāro nāsamudācāraḥ, na smṛtimān nāsmṛtimān, na cetano na niścetanaḥ, na mano nāmanaḥ, na nirjāto nānirjātaḥ, na nāmo nānāmaḥ, na rūpo nārūpaḥ, na vyāhāro nāvyāhāraḥ, na prajñapyo nāprajñapyaḥ, na dṛśyo nādṛśyaḥ, na netrī nānetrī, na mārgapraṇetā nāmārgapraṇetā, na prāptaphalo nāprāptaphalaḥ, na kalpo nākalpaḥ, na kalpāpagato nākalpāpagataḥ /
children.translated_text: nor non-acting, neither manifesting nor non-manifesting, neither mindful nor non-mindful, neither conscious nor unconscious, neither with mind nor without mind, neither arisen nor non-arisen, neither named nor unnamed, neither with form nor without form, neither speaking nor non-speaking, neither designated nor non-designated, neither visible nor invisible, neither a guide nor a non-guide, neither a path-establisher nor a non-path-establisher, neither one who has attained the fruit nor one who has not attained the fruit, neither a <s>kalpa</s> (eon) nor a non-<s>kalpa</s>, neither free from <s>kalpas</s> nor not free from <s>kalpas</s>.

body.translated_text: In the same way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, also does not construct, does not conceptualize, does not think, does not deliberate. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is devoid of mind, thought, and consciousness — unborn, unceased, without marks, free from marks, without mental activity, free from mental activity, without conceptual proliferation, free from conceptual proliferation, without burning, free from burning; neither here nor there, neither high nor low, neither bound nor liberated, neither possessing knowledge nor lacking knowledge, neither defiled nor purified, neither speaking truth nor speaking falsehood, neither on this shore nor the far shore, neither on the bank nor off the bank, neither in the depths nor not in the depths, neither on dry land nor not on dry land, neither in a flood nor not in a flood, neither omniscient nor non-omniscient, neither reasoned nor unreasoned, neither acting

body.text: atha ca punar mañjuśrīs tathāgatasūryamaṇḍalajñānaraśmayas traidhātuke 'nantamadhyadharmadhātvapratihataraśmyavabhāsapramuktāḥ / prasṛtāś ca raśmayaḥ pūrvataram eva mahāśailendrakalpādhyāśayānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ kāye nipatanti / tataḥ paścāt pratyekabuddhayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ kāye nipatanti / tataḥ paścāc chrāvakayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ kāye nipatanti / tataḥ paścāt kuśalādhyāśayānāṃ yathādhimuktīnāṃ sattvānāṃ kāye nipatanti / tataḥ paścād antaśo mithyātvaniyateṣu sattvasaṃtāneṣu kāye tathāgatasūryamaṇḍalaraśmayo nipatanti / teṣāṃ copakārībhūtā bhavanty anāgatahetusaṃjananatayā, saṃvardhayanti ca kuśalair dharmaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the rays of knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> (solar disc), released as the radiance of rays unobstructed in the infinite, middleless <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Reality) throughout the three realms, have gone forth. And those rays fall first upon the bodies of <s>bodhisattvas</s> whose aspirations are like the great king of mountains; then afterward they fall upon the bodies of those who have set out in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle; then afterward they fall upon the bodies of those who have set out in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (Hearer) vehicle; then afterward they fall upon the bodies of beings with wholesome aspirations according to their faith-inclinations; then afterward, the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> fall even upon the bodies of those in the continua of beings who are fixed in wrong views. And they become beneficial to them by generating causes for the future, and they nourish them with wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatra ca tathāgato mañjuśrīḥ samaḥ sarvatropekṣako nirvikalpo nirviśeṣaḥ / na punar mañjuśrīs tathāgatajñānasūryamaṇḍalasyaivaṃ bhavati / asyāhaṃ sattvasyodāraṃ (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 40]

children.text: ) dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmi, asya na deśayiṣyāmīti / na tasyaivaṃ vikalpo bhavati, ayam udārādhimuktikaḥ sattvaḥ, ayaṃ madhyādhimuktikaḥ, ayaṃ śrāvakayānādhimuktikaḥ / ayaṃ kuśalāśayaḥ, ayaṃ hīno mithyāśaya iti /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, and to this one I shall not teach.' No such conceptual construction arises in it [as]: 'This being has lofty faith-inclination, this one has middling faith-inclination, this one has faith-inclination toward the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle; this one has wholesome aspiration, this one is inferior and has wrong aspiration.'

body.translated_text: And therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is equal, impartial toward all, free from conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), without distinction. Nor, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge think thus: 'To this being I shall teach the excellent

body.text: na mañjuśrīs tathāgatajñānasūryamaṇḍalasyaivaṃ bhavati / ayam udārāśayādhimuktikaḥ sattvo 'sya mahāyānaṃ deśayiṣyāmi, ayaṃ madhyāśayādhimukto 'sya pratyekabuddhayānaṃ deśayiṣyāmi, ayaṃ śrāvakayānādhimuktiko 'sya śrāvakayānaṃ deśayiṣyāmi / kuśalākuśalāśayānāṃ ca sattvānām āśayaṃ viditvā viśodhayiṣyāmi, ṛjukāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ kariṣyāmi / yāvad mithyātvaniyatānām api sattvānāṃ yathānurūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmi / na tathāgatajñānasūryamaṇḍalaraśmyavabhāsasyaivaṃ vikalpo bhavati / tat kasya hetoḥ / sarvakalpavikalpaprapañcasamucchinnatvāt tathāgatajñānasūryamaṇḍalaraśmyavabhāsasya / atha ca mañjuśrīḥ sattvānāṃ kuśalāśayasaṃtānavaicitryāt tathāgatajñānasūryamaṇḍalaraśmyavabhāsasya vaicitryaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Nor, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, does the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge think thus: 'This being has lofty aspiration and faith-inclination — to this one I shall teach the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle); this one has middling aspiration and faith-inclination — to this one I shall teach the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle; this one has faith-inclination toward the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle — to this one I shall teach the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle; and having known the aspirations of beings with wholesome and unwholesome dispositions, I shall purify them, I shall make their view straight; and I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> appropriately even to beings who are fixed in wrong views.' No such conceptual construction arises in the radiance of the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge. Why is that? Because the radiance of the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge has completely cut off all constructions, conceptual elaborations, and proliferations. And yet, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, due to the diversity in the continua of beings' wholesome aspirations, there arises diversity in the radiance of the rays of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sun-<s>maṇḍala</s> of knowledge.

body.text: tadyathā mañjuśrīr asti mahāsāgare sarvābhiprāyaparipūraṇaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ tad dhvajāgrāvabaddham / yasya sattvasya yādṛśo 'bhiprāyo bhavati, tādṛśaṃ tataḥ (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 41]

children.text: ) śabdaṃ niścarantaṃ sattvāḥ saṃjānanti / tac ca mahāmaṇiratnaṃ na kalpayati na vikalpayati na cintayati na vicintayati, acintyaṃ niścintyaṃ cittamanovijñānāpagatam /
children.translated_text: [continuation of previous segment]

body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there exists in the great ocean a great gem-jewel called 'Fulfiller of All Wishes' (<s>sarvābhiprāyaparipūraṇa</s>), fastened atop a banner-pole. Whatever kind of wish a being has, from that [jewel] beings perceive a sound of that very kind issuing forth. And that great gem-jewel does not construct, does not conceptually elaborate, does not think, does not deliberate — it is unthinkable, beyond thought, gone beyond mind, mentation, and consciousness.

body.text: evam eva mañjuśrīs tathāgato na kalpayati na vikalpayati na cintayati na vicintayati, na cintyo niścintyaś cittamanovijñānāpagataḥ / agrāho 'paryavagrāhaḥ, aprāpto 'prāptavyaḥ, praṇunnapratyekasatyaḥ, praṇunnarāgaḥ praṇunnadoṣaḥ praṇunnamohaḥ, na satyo na mṛṣā, na nityo nānityaḥ, na prabho nāprabhaḥ, na loko nālokaḥ, avitarko 'vicāraḥ, anutpanno 'niruddhaḥ / acintyo 'pracintyaḥ, asvabhāvo 'svābhāvyaḥ, abhāvaśūnyaḥ, anāyūho 'niryūhaḥ, anabhiniveśyaḥ, avyavahāro vyavahārasamucchedaḥ, anānando nirānando nandīsamudghātaḥ, asaṃkhyātaḥ saṃkhyāpagataḥ, agatir agatigāmī sarvagatisamucchinnaḥ, sarvavyāhārasamucchinnaḥ, adṛśyo 'nālokyo 'grāhyaḥ, nāvakāśo nānavakāśaḥ, na paśyo na nirdeśyaḥ, na sāmagrī na visāmagrī, na vikalpito nāvikalpitaḥ, aviṭhāpito 'saṃdarśitaḥ, asaṃkliṣṭo 'pariśodhanārhaḥ, na nāma na rūpaṃ na nimittam, na karma na karmavipākaḥ, nātīto (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 42]

children.text: ) nānāgato na pratyutpannaḥ, niṣkiñcanaḥ, araṇaḥ, anakṣaraḥ, aghoṣo ghoṣasamatikrānto 'rutaḥ, alakṣaṇaḥ sarvalakṣaṇāpagataḥ, nādhyātmyaṃ na bahirddhā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate / atha ca mañjuśrīs tathāgatajñānaratnam adhyāśayapariśuddhaṃ mahākaruṇādhvajāgrāvabaddham, tato yo yathāśayādhimuktaḥ sattvaḥ sa tathā dharmadeśanāṃ niścarantīṃ saṃjānāti / tatra ca tathāgataḥ samaḥ sarvatropekṣako nirvikalpo nirviśeṣaḥ //
