This being has middling dispositions and aspirations — I shall give this being a discourse on the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. This being has sublime dispositions and aspirations — I shall give this being a discourse on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.'

body.translated_text: In just this way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, should it be understood regarding the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. This does not occur to the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'This being has inferior aspirations;

body.text: na mañjuśrīs tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati / ayam udārādhimuktaḥ sattvaḥ, asya sattvasya dānakathāṃ kariṣye //
body.translated_text: This does not occur to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'This being has sublime aspirations — I shall give this being a discourse on generosity (<s>dāna</s>).'

body.text: evaṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntiṃ vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ ca / na mañjuśrīs tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati / ayaṃ prajñāpāramitādhimuktaḥ sattvaḥ, asya sattvasya prajñāpāramitāṃ kathāṃ kathayiṣye / naivaṃ mañjuśrīs tathāgatasyaivaṃ bhavati / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / dharmakāyo mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ / atyantānutpanno mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ //
body.translated_text: Likewise regarding morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). This does not occur to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>: 'This being has aspirations toward the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) — I shall teach this being a discourse on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' It does not occur thus to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. Why is that? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body). The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is ultimately unborn.

body.text: na mañjuśrīs tathāgatasya nāmarūpaniruktyānusāri vijñānaṃ pravartate / na mañjuśrīs tathāgataḥ kalpayati, na vikalpayati / kṣaṇiko hi mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'kṣayalakṣaṇo 'kṣayakoṭībhūtakoṭīniyataḥ //
body.translated_text: The consciousness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, does not operate following the etymological analysis of name and form. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, does not construct, does not discriminate. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is momentary, with the characteristic of inexhaustibility, determined at the limit of inexhaustible koṭis.

body.text: sarvadharmasamatākoṭī mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddhaḥ samaḥ sarvatra nirvikalpo nirviśeṣaḥ, na hīno na madhyo notkṛṣṭaḥ / evam eva mañjuśrīḥ samāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, nirvikalpā nirviśeṣāḥ, na hīnā na madhyā notkṛṣṭāḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / anupalabdhitvāt sarvadharmāṇām / yā mañjuśrīr anupalabdhiḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sā samatā, yā samatā sā sthitā, yā sthitā sācalanatā, yācalanatā sāniśrayatā //
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the limit of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> — equal everywhere, free from conceptual elaboration, without differentiation, neither inferior nor middling nor superior. In just this way, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are equal, free from conceptual elaboration, without differentiation, neither inferior nor middling nor superior. Why is that? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are unapprehensible. That which, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the unapprehensibility of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is their equality; that which is equality — that is their stability; that which is stability — that is their immovability; that which is immovability — that is their state of being without support.

body.text: aniśritasya sarvadharmeṣu nāsti cittapratiṣṭhānam / apratiṣṭhitacittasyānutpattir ājāyate / evaṃ darśinaś ca viparyastāc cittacaitasikā na pravartante / yaś cāviparyastacittaḥ sa yathāvatprāpto bhavati / yathāvatprāpto na prapañcayati / aprapañcayataḥ pracāro nāsti / yadā na pracarati tadā na saṃcarati / yadā na saṃcarati tadā na visarati / avisaraṃ dharmatāṃ na virodhayati / dharmatām avirodhayan sarvatrānulomo bhavati / sarvatrānulomo dharmaprakṛter na calati / dharmaprakṛter acalaṃ dharmaprakṛtiprāpto bhavati / dharmaprakṛtiprāpto na kiṃcit prapañcayati / tat kasya hetoḥ / pratyayahetujanitatvāt //
body.translated_text: For one without support, there is no establishment of mind in any <s>dharma</s>. For one whose mind is unestablished, non-arising arises. For one who sees thus, the perverted mind and mental factors do not operate. One whose mind is unperverted becomes one who has arrived at reality as it is. One who has arrived at reality as it is does not engage in proliferation. For one who does not engage in proliferation, there is no activity. When there is no activity, there is no wandering about. When there is no wandering about, there is no straying. One who does not stray does not oppose <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality). One who does not oppose <s>dharmatā</s> becomes conformable to everything. One conformable to everything does not deviate from the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. One who does not deviate from the nature of <s>dharmas</s> has attained the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. One who has attained the nature of <s>dharmas</s> does not engage in any proliferation. Why is that? Because it is produced from conditions and causes.

body.text: yaḥ pratyayahetujanitaḥ so 'tyantājātaḥ / yaś cātyantājātaḥ (

children.translated_text: JĀA 49

children.text: ) sa niyāmaprāptaḥ / yaś ca niyāmaprāptaḥ sa sarvadharmamanasikāraiḥ sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati / yadā sarvadharmamanasikāraiḥ sārdhaṃ na saṃvasati tadā saṃvāśyo na bhavati / yadā saṃvāśyo na bhavati tadā na bhavati na vibhavati / yadā na bhavati na vibhavati tadā sthito dharmaprāpto bhavati / yadā sthito dharmaprāpto bhavati tadā yoniśodharmaprayukto bhavati / yoniśodharmaprayuktasya na kaścid dharmo 'sti yo na buddhadharmaḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ / śūnyatānubodhatvāt / yaś ca śūnyatānubodhaḥ sa bodhiḥ //
children.translated_text: has attained the <s>niyāma</s> (certainty of correctness). One who has attained <s>niyāma</s> does not dwell together with mental engagements regarding any <s>dharma</s>. When one does not dwell together with mental engagements regarding any <s>dharma</s>, one does not become a co-dweller. When one does not become a co-dweller, one neither comes into being nor ceases to be. When one neither comes into being nor ceases to be, one becomes established, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>. When one becomes established, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, one becomes rightly engaged in the <s>Dharma</s>. For one rightly engaged in the <s>Dharma</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that is not a <s>Buddha-dharma</s>. Why is that? Because of the awakening to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). That which is the awakening to <s>śūnyatā</s> — that is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

body.translated_text: That which is produced from conditions and causes is ultimately unborn. That which is ultimately unborn

body.text: sa evaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārāniketāsaṃbhavāgrāhyānālayāvabodhād bodhiḥ / bodhiś ca yoniśoprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, from the awakening to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness), <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness), non-formation, non-abode, non-arising, ungraspability, and non-attachment — that is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). And <s>bodhi</s> is right engagement.

body.text: yoniśaḥprayogaḥ, yoniśaḥ prayogenāmocyate / anupekṣāprakṣepaḥ, akāravikāraprayogaḥ, asaṃbaddhaḥ, apramuktaprayogaḥ, anekatvānānātvaprayogaḥ, anāgataprayogo yoniśaḥ prayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Right engagement — by right engagement one is not released. It is without disregard or casting away, without change of form or transformation in practice, unconnected, without release in practice, practicing neither oneness nor manyness, practicing the not-yet-come — this is right engagement.

body.text: na tatra prayogo na pramāṇaṃ na phalasākṣātkriyā / tat kasya hetoḥ / prakṛtiprabhāsvaraṃ cittaṃ tac cāgantukair upakleśair upakliśyate na ca prakṛtiḥ saṃkliśyate / yā ca prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā sāsaṃkleśatā / yā cāsaṃkleśatā tatra pratipakṣo nāsti yena pratipakṣeṇa kleśaprahāṇaṃ syāt / tat (

children.translated_text: JĀA 50

children.text: ) kasya hetoḥ / na śuddhaḥ śudhyati śuddha eva saḥ / yaś ca śuddhaḥ so 'nutpādaḥ / yaś cānutpādaḥ so 'ninditaḥ / yaś cāninditaḥ sa nandīprahāṇaṃ tatra sarvasnehā nirudhyante / yatra sarvasnehā nirudhyante so 'nutpādaḥ / yaś cānutpādaḥ sa bodhiḥ //
children.translated_text: is that? Because the pure is not purified — it is already pure. That which is pure is unborn. That which is unborn is blameless. That which is blameless — therein delight is abandoned and all attachment ceases. Where all attachment ceases — that is non-arising. That which is non-arising — that is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

body.translated_text: Therein there is no practice, no measure, and no direct realization of the fruit. Why is that? Because the mind is luminous by nature, and it is defiled by adventitious defilements — yet the [original] nature is not defiled. That which is the natural luminosity — that is the state of non-defilement. That which is the state of non-defilement — therein there is no antidote by which there could be an abandonment of defilements. Why

body.text: yā bodhiḥ sā samatā / yā samatā sā tathatā / tathatāpratiṣṭhitāś ca sarvadharmāḥ saṃskṛtā asaṃskṛtāś ca / yā ca tathatā na tatra saṃskṛtaṃ nāsaṃskṛtaṃ na dvayaprajñaptiḥ / yatra na saṃskṛtaṃ nāsaṃskṛtaṃ na dvayaprajñaptiḥ sā tathatā / yā tathatā sānanyatathatā / yānanyatathatā sāvikāratathatā / yā cāvikāratathatā sānāgatatathatā / yā cānāgatatathatā sāvitathatā / yā cāvitathatā sā yathāvattathatā / yā yathāvattathatā sā najātutathatā / yā najātutathatā sā na saṃkliśyate na viśudhyate / yā na saṃkliśyate na viśudhyate sā notpadyate na nirudhyate / yā notpadyate na nirudhyate sā nirvāṇena samā / yā nirvāṇena samā sā na saṃsarati na parinirvāti / yā na saṃsarati na parinirvāti sā nātītā nānāgatā na pratyutpannā / yā nātītā nānāgatā na pratyutpannā sā na hīnā na madhyā notkṛṣṭā / yā na hīnā na madhyā notkṛṣṭā sā tathatā //
body.translated_text: That which is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is sameness (<s>samatā</s>). That which is sameness is suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). And all <s>dharmas</s>, conditioned and unconditioned, are established in suchness. In that suchness there is neither the conditioned nor the unconditioned, nor the designation of duality. Where there is neither the conditioned nor the unconditioned, nor the designation of duality — that is suchness. That which is suchness is non-other-suchness. That which is non-other-suchness is unchanging suchness. And that which...

body.text: tathatā nāmocyate / tattvārthādhivacanam etat tattvam (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 51]

children.text: ) ucyate / tathātvaṃ tathatvam ucyate / tathaiva tathatā cātmā cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram / yaś cādvayārthaḥ sa bodhiś cāvabodhārthaḥ//
children.translated_text: is spoken of. 'Such-ness' means 'being-such.' Suchness, the Self, and non-duality — this is non-division. And that which is the meaning of non-duality, that is <s>bodhi</s> — the meaning of awakening.

body.translated_text: is called suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). This is a designation for the meaning of reality (<s>tattva</s>). Reality (<s>tattva</s>)

body.text: artha ucyate / trivimokṣamukhapraveśaṃ jñānaṃ sarvadharmanirdeśeṣu / jñānam ucyate / tryadhvasamatāvatāraḥ sarvadharmeṣu / asaṃbhedārthaś ca sarvadharmāṇām ayam ucyate 'rthaḥ / aruto 'nabhilāpyo 'vyāhāro vyāhārasamucchinnaḥ //
body.translated_text: The meaning is stated: knowledge that enters the three gates of liberation (<s>trivimokṣamukha</s>) in all teachings of the <s>Dharma</s>. Knowledge is stated: the entry into the sameness of the three times regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. And the meaning of the non-differentiation of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is called 'meaning.' It is soundless, inexpressible, beyond utterance, with utterance cut off.

body.text: jñānam ucyate / yad arthānugamajñānaṃ vijñānānugamaṃ cedam ucyate jñānam / artha ucyate / yat tattvārthajñānena vijñānānugamajñānena ca nītārthatā / saiva dharmatā yā / yā ca dharmatā so 'rthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Knowledge is stated: that knowledge which follows meaning, and that which follows consciousness — this is called knowledge. Meaning is stated: that which is definitive meaning, [established] through knowledge of reality and through knowledge that follows consciousness. That very <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) — that which is <s>dharmatā</s>, that is the meaning.

body.text: yārthānugamajñānena vijñānānugamajñānena nītārthānugamajñānena ca sā dharmatā / yā dharmatā so 'rthaḥ / sā ca dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmaniyāmatā, sā dharme na pravartate / yā dharmasyāpravṛttiḥ, yā cārthavyaṃjanasamatā sādvayārthe samā / yā ca samatā so 'rthaḥ, sā cārthajñānena samatā, sādvayamukhapraveśena jñānasamatā //
body.translated_text: Through knowledge that follows meaning, through knowledge that follows consciousness, and through knowledge that follows definitive meaning — that is <s>dharmatā</s>. That which is <s>dharmatā</s>, that is the meaning. And that <s>dharmatā</s> is the stability of <s>dharma</s>, the fixed order of <s>dharma</s>; it does not operate in <s>dharma</s>. That which is the non-operation of <s>dharma</s>, and that which is the sameness of meaning and expression — that is equal in the non-dual meaning. That which is sameness, that is the meaning; and that sameness through knowledge of meaning — that is the non-dual...

body.text: nītārthena neyārthasamatā samānārthā sā śūnyatā / samānārthena pudgalasamatā samā / pudgalasamatayā dharmasamatā samā / dharmasamatayā vimuktisamatā samā / vimuktisamatayā cānubodho bodhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Through the definitive meaning, the sameness of the provisional meaning is of equal meaning — that is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Through the equal meaning, the sameness of the person (<s>pudgala</s>) is equal. Through the sameness of the person, the sameness of <s>dharmas</s> is equal. Through the sameness of <s>dharmas</s>, the sameness of liberation is equal. Through the sameness of liberation, awakening is <s>bodhi</s>.

body.text: rūpasaṅgasaṃyuktānāṃ mañjuśrīś cakṣuḥ saṅgaḥ / rūpacakṣuḥprakṛtijñānam asaṅgaḥ / dṛṣṭisaṅgasaṃyuktānāṃ svakāyaṃ saṅgaḥ / sarvadṛṣṭikṛtānāṃ svakāyaprakṛtiś[ṭā̆]ūnyatājñānam asaṅgaḥ / ayoniśomanaskārasaṅgasaktānāṃ dharmālokaḥ saṅgaḥ / yoniśomanaskāradharmapratyavekṣāprakṛtiśūnyatāsvabhāvaśūnyatājñānam asaṅgaḥ / vicikitsāmalasaṅgasaktānāṃ mokṣaḥ saṅgaḥ / adhimuktivimuktiyathābhūtajñānam asaṅgaḥ / kauśīdyamalasaṅgasaktānām adhigamadṛṣṭavīryatā saṅgaḥ / yathādharmāṇām anubodhaḥ saṅgaḥ / nīvaraṇasaṅgayuktānāṃ bodhyaṅgāni saṅgaḥ / anāvaraṇajñānavimokṣo 'saṃgaḥ //
body.translated_text: For those bound by attachment to form, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the eye is the attachment. Knowledge of the intrinsic nature of form and the eye is non-attachment. For those bound by attachment to views, one's own body is the attachment. Knowledge of the intrinsic emptiness of one's own body for all view-formations is non-attachment. For those bound by attachment to improper mental attention, the light of the <s>Dharma</s> is the attachment. Knowledge of the intrinsic emptiness and self-nature emptiness of proper mental attention and <s>Dharma</s>-investigation is non-attachment.

body.text: prakṛtipariśuddhāḥ sarvadharmā hetupratyayasāmagryā pravartante / tatra bodhisattvena saṃkleśahetur vyavadānahetuś ca parijñātavyaḥ / saṃkleśahetuviśuddhyā ca vyavadānaviśuddhyā ca na sthātavyam//
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are intrinsically pure; they operate through the assembly of causes and conditions. Therein, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should fully understand the cause of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and the cause of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). And one should not abide in either the purification of the cause of defilement or the purification of purification.

body.text: ātmasamutthānaṃ ca saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / nairātmyadharmāvatārakṣāntir vyavadānasya hetuḥ / ahaṃkāramamakāradṛṣṭiḥ saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / adhyātmopaśamo bahirdhāpacāraś ca vyavadānasya hetuḥ / kāmavyāpādavihiṃsāvitarkaḥ (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 53]

children.text: ) saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / aśubhāmaitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāpratītyadharmāvatārakṣāntir vyavadānasya hetuḥ / catvāro viparyāsāḥ saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / catvāri samyaksmṛtyupasthānāni vyavadānasya hetuḥ / pañca nīvaraṇāni saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / pañcendriyāṇi vyavadānasya hetuḥ / ṣaḍ āyatanāni saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / ṣaḍ anusmṛtayo vyavadānasya hetuḥ / saptāsaddharmāḥ saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / sapta bodhyaṅgāni vyavadānasya hetuḥ / aṣṭa mithyātvāni saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / aṣṭau samyaktvāni vyavadānasya hetuḥ / navāghātavastūni saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayo vyavadānasya hetuḥ / daśākuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ saṃkleśasya hetuḥ / daśa kuśalāḥ karmapathā vyavadānasya hetuḥ / saṃkṣiptena sarve 'kuśalā manaskārāḥ saṃkleśasya hetuḥ, sarve kuśalā manaskārā vyavadānasya hetuḥ //
children.translated_text: are the cause of defilement. Patient acceptance of the entry into <s>dharmas</s> of the foul, loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity, and dependent origination is the cause of purification. The four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) are the cause of defilement. The four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) are the cause of purification. The five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>) are the cause of defilement. The five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) are the cause of purification. The six sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) are the cause of defilement. The six...

body.translated_text: The arising from the self is the cause of defilement. Patient acceptance of the entry into the <s>dharma</s> of non-self is the cause of purification. The view of 'I' and 'mine' is the cause of defilement. Inner tranquility and outer non-misconduct is the cause of purification. Thoughts of desire, ill-will, and harm

body.text: tatra yaḥ saṃkleśasya hetuḥ, yaś ca vyavadānasya hetuḥ, sarve te dharmāḥ prakṛtiśūnyā niḥsattvā nirjīvā niṣpoṣā niṣpuruṣā niṣpudgalā asvāmikā aparigrahā nirvyāpārā māyopamā alakṣaṇā adhyātmopaśāntāḥ / yaś cādhyātmopaśamaḥ sa praśamaḥ / yaḥ praśamaḥ sā prakṛtiḥ / yā prakṛtiḥ so 'nupalambhaḥ / yo 'nupalambhaḥ so 'nilayaḥ / yaś cānilayaḥ tat kham / khaṃ cākāśam / sa ākāśasamān sarvadharmān prajānāti, saṃkleśavyavadānena ca vyavaharati, na cākāśadharmatāṃ vijahāti / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na kaścin mañjuśrīr dharmaḥ saṃvidyate yasyotpādo nirodho vā bhavet //
body.translated_text: Therein, that which is the cause of defilement and that which is the cause of purification — all those <s>dharmas</s> are intrinsically empty, devoid of beings, devoid of life, devoid of sustenance, devoid of personhood, devoid of a self (<s>pudgala</s>), without an owner, without possession, without activity, like a magical illusion, without characteristics, inwardly tranquil. And that which is inner tranquility is pacification. That which is pacification is the intrinsic nature. That which is the intrinsic nature is non-apprehension. That which is non-apprehension...

body.text: mañjuśrīr āha / tat kathaṃ bhagavaṃs tathāgatena bodhiḥ prāptā / bhagavān āha / amūlāpratiṣṭhānā mañjuśrīs tathāgatena bodhiḥ prāptā / mañjuśrīr āha / tatra katamad bhagavan mūlaṃ katamat pratiṣṭhānam / bhagavān āha / satkāyo mañjuśrīr mūlam abhūtaparikalpaḥ pratiṣṭhānam / tat tathāgatena mañjuśrīr bodhisamatayā sarvadharmasamatā jñātā / tasmād ucyate mañjuśrīr amūlāpratiṣṭhānā tathāgatena bodhir abhisaṃbuddheti //
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'How then, Blessed One, was <s>bodhi</s> attained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>bodhi</s> was attained by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as rootless and without foundation.' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'What then, Blessed One, is the root? What is the foundation?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the identity-view (<s>satkāya</s>) is the root; false conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is the foundation. That, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>...'

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīḥ śāntā copaśāntā ca / tatra katamaḥ śamaḥ katama upaśamaḥ / adhyātmaṃ śamaḥ, bahirdhopaśamaḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / cakśur mañjuśrīḥ śūnyam ātmanā cātmīyena ca, prakṛtir asyaiṣā, ayam ucyate śama iti / sa cakṣuḥ śūnyam iti parijñāya rūpeṣu na dhāvati, tenocyata upaśama iti /
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is tranquil and pacified. Therein, what is tranquility (<s>śama</s>) and what is pacification (<s>upaśama</s>)? Internally is tranquility; externally is pacification. And why? The eye, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is empty of self and of what belongs to self; this is its intrinsic nature — this is called 'tranquility.' Having fully understood that the eye is empty, one does not run after forms — therefore it is called 'pacification.'

body.text: evaṃ śrotraṃ śūnyam ātmanā cātmīyena ca, prakṛtir asyaiṣā, ayam ucyate śama iti / sa śrotraṃ śūnyam iti parijñāya śabdeṣu na dhāvati, tenocyata upaśama iti /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the ear is empty of self and of what belongs to self; this is its intrinsic nature — this is called 'tranquility.' Having fully understood that the ear is empty, one does not run after sounds — therefore it is called 'pacification.'

body.text: ghrāṇaṃ śūnyam ātmanā cātmīyena ca, prakṛtir asyaiṣā, ayam ucyate śama iti / sa ghrāṇaṃ śūnyam iti parijñāya gandheṣu na dhāvati, tenocyata upaśama iti /
body.translated_text: The nose is empty of self and of what belongs to self; this is its intrinsic nature — this is called 'tranquility.' Having fully understood that the nose is empty, one does not run after smells — therefore it is called 'pacification.'

body.text: jihvā śūnyātmanā cātmīyena ca, prakṛtir asyā eṣā, ayam ucyate śama iti / sa jihvā śūnyeti parijñāya raseṣu na (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 55]
therefore it is called 'pacification.'

body.translated_text: The tongue is empty of self and of what belongs to self; this is its intrinsic nature — this is called 'tranquility.' Having fully understood that the tongue is empty, one does not run after tastes —

body.text: kāyaḥ śūnya ātmanā cātmīyena ca, prakṛtir asyaiṣā, ayam ucyate śama iti / sa kāyaṃ śūnyam iti parijñāya spraṣṭavyeṣu na dhāvati, tenocyata upaśama iti /
body.translated_text: The body is empty of self and of what belongs to self; this is its intrinsic nature — this is called 'tranquility.' Having fully understood that the body is empty, one does not run after tangibles — therefore it is called 'pacification.'

body.text: mano mañjuśrīḥ śūnyam ātmanā cātmīyena ca, prakṛtir asyaiṣā, ayam ucyate śama iti / sa manaḥ śūnyam iti parijñāya dharmeṣu na dhāvati, tenocyata upaśama iti //
body.translated_text: The mind, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is empty of self and of what belongs to a self; this is its nature — this is called <s>śama</s> (quiescence). One who, having fully understood that the mind is empty, does not chase after <s>dharmas</s> — that is why it is called <s>upaśama</s> (deep quiescence).

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīḥ prakṛtiprabhāsvarā cittaprakṛtiprabhāsvaratayā / tena kāraṇenocyate prakṛtiprabhāsvareti / yā sā prakṛti sāsaṃkliṣṭā, ākāśasamā, ākāśaprakṛtiḥ, ākāśasamavasaraṇā, ākāśopamā, atyantaprabhāsvarā prakṛtiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is naturally luminous, because the nature of mind is luminous. For that reason it is called 'naturally luminous.' That nature is undefiled, equal to space, of the nature of space, having space as its abode, comparable to space — a nature utterly luminous.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr anāyūhāniryūhā / tatra katamānāyūhatā katamāniryūhatā / anāyūhas tenocyate 'grahaḥ sarvadharmāṇām / aniryūha ucyate 'nutsargaḥ sarvadharmāṇām / tatra mañjuśrīs tathāgato 'nāyūho 'niryūha ogham avatārṣīt / tathā cāvatārṣīd yathā tathatāyā nāpāraṃ na pāraṃ samanupaśyati / iti hy apārapāravigatāḥ sarvadharmās tathāgatenābhisaṃbuddhāḥ / tena tathāgata ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is without accumulation and without release. Therein, what is the state of non-accumulation and what is the state of non-release? Non-accumulation — by this is meant the non-grasping of all <s>dharmas</s>. Non-release is called the non-abandonment of all <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, without accumulating and without releasing, crossed the flood. And he crossed it in such a way that he does not perceive either a near shore or a far shore of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). For all <s>dharmas</s>, being beyond near and far shores, have been perfectly awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore he is called '<s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr animittānārambaṇā / tatra katamānimittatā katamānārambaṇatā / cakṣurvijñānānupalabdhir mañjuśrīr animittatā / rūpasyāsamanupaśyanatānārambaṇatā / śrotravijñānānupalabdhir animittatā / śabdāśravaṇatānārambaṇatā/ ghrāṇavijñānānupalabdhir animittatā / gandhāghrāṇatānārambaṇatā / jihvāvijñānānupalabdhir animittatā / rasāsvādanatānārambaṇatā / kāyavijñānānupalabdhir animittatā / spraṣṭavyāspṛśaṇatānārambaṇatā / manovijñānānupalabdhir animittatā / dharmāvijñānatānārambaṇatā / ayaṃ mañjuśrīr āryāṇāṃ gocaraḥ / yas traidhātuke 'gocaraḥ, ayaṃ mañjuśrīr āryāṇāṃ gocaraḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is signless and without support. Therein, what is signlessness and what is supportlessness? The non-apprehension of eye-consciousness, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is signlessness; the non-perception of form is supportlessness. The non-apprehension of ear-consciousness is signlessness; the non-hearing of sound is supportlessness. The non-apprehension of nose-consciousness is signlessness; the non-smelling of odor is supportlessness. The non-apprehension of tongue-consciousness is signlessness; the non-tasting of flavor is supportlessness. The non-apprehension of body-consciousness is signlessness; the non-touching of tangibles is supportlessness. The non-apprehension of mind-consciousness is signlessness; the non-cognizing of <s>dharmas</s> is supportlessness. This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the domain of the Noble Ones. That which is the non-domain in the three realms — this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the domain of the Noble Ones.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr nātītā nānāgatā na pratyutpannā tryadhvasamā trimaṇḍalaparicchinnā / tatra katamo mañjuśrīs trimaṇḍalaparicchedaḥ / yad atīte cittaṃ nopalabhyate / anāgate vijñānaṃ na dhāvati / na pratyutpanne manaskāraḥ pravartate / sa cittamanovijñānāpratiṣṭhito na kalpayati na vikalpayati / anavakalpayann avikalpayan nātītaṃ karoty anāgataṃ na manyate pratyutpannaṃ na prapañcayati //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is neither past, nor future, nor present — equal with the three times, delimited by three spheres. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is the delimitation by three spheres? The mind in the past is not apprehended. Consciousness does not run toward the future. Mental engagement does not operate in the present. One who is established in neither mind, thought, nor consciousness does not construct and does not discriminate. Not constructing and not discriminating, one does not make the past, does not conceive the future, and does not proliferate about the present.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr aśarīrāsaṃskṛtā / tatrāśarīratā mañjuśrīr yā na cakṣurvijñānavijñeyā, na śrotra, na ghrāṇa, na jihvā, na kāya, na manovijñānavijñeyā / yan mañjuśrīr na cittamanovijñānavijñeyaṃ tad asaṃskṛtam / asaṃskṛtam ucyate yatra notpādo na sthitir na vyayaḥ / tad ucyate trimaṇḍalapariśuddham asaṃskṛtam / yathaivāsaṃskṛtas tathaivaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ boddhavyam / tat kasya hetoḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ yaḥ svabhāvaḥ so 'svabhāvaḥ, tatra nāsti dvayam iti //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is bodiless and unconditioned. Therein, bodilessness, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is that which is not cognizable by eye-consciousness, nor by ear, nose, tongue, body, nor by mind-consciousness. That, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, which is not cognizable by mind, thought, and consciousness is the unconditioned. The unconditioned is called that in which there is no arising, no abiding, and no passing away. That is called the unconditioned, purified in three spheres. Just as the unconditioned is, so should the conditioned be understood. Why? Because the self-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is non-self-nature; therein there is no duality.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr abhedapadam etat / tatra katamo 'bhedaḥ, katamat padam / asaṃjñābhedas tathatā padam / apratiṣṭhānam abhedo dharmadhātuḥ padam / anānātvam abhedo bhūtakoṭiḥ padam / anilambho 'bhedo 'calanatā padam / śūnyatābhedo 'nimittaṃ padam / avitarko 'bhedo 'praṇihitaṃ padam / aprārthanābhedo niḥsattvatā padam / sattvāsvabhāvo 'bheda ākāśaṃ padam / anupalambho 'bhedo 'nutpādaṃ padam / anirodho 'bhedo 'saṃskṛtaṃ padam / apracāro 'bhedo bodhiḥ padam / vyupaśamo 'bhedo nirvāṇaṃ padam / anabhinirvṛttir abhedo 'jātiḥ padam //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the station of non-division. Therein, what is non-division and what is the station? Non-division of perception — <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is the station. Non-establishment is the non-division — <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of <s>dharmas</s>) is the station. Non-differentiation is the non-division — <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) is the station. Non-grasping is the non-division — immovability is the station. Non-division of emptiness — the signless is the station. Non-deliberation is the non-division — the wishless is the station. Non-seeking is the non-division — the absence of beings is the station. The non-self-nature of beings is the non-division — space is the station. Non-apprehension is the non-division — non-arising is the station. Non-ceasing is the non-division — the unconditioned is the station. Non-activity is the non-division — <s>bodhi</s> is the station. Complete quiescence is the non-division — <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the station. Non-production is the non-division — non-birth is the station.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr na kāyenābhisambudhyate na cittena / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / jaḍaḥ kāyo mañjuśrīr niśceṣṭo 'cetanas tṛṇakāṣṭhakuḍyaloṣṭapratibhāsopamaḥ / cittaṃ ca māyopamaṃ riktaṃ tuccham abhūtam asaṃskṛtam / yo mañjuśrīr evaṃ kāyasya cittasya cāvabodhaḥ, ayam ucyate mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ / vyavahāram upādāya na punaḥ paramārthataḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ kāyena vā cittena vā dharmeṇa vā adharmeṇa vā bhūtena vābhūtena vā satyena vā mṛṣā vā vacanīyā //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is not awakened to by the body nor by the mind. Why? The body, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is inert, motionless, without consciousness — comparable to grass, wood, a wall, or a clod of earth, comparable to a reflection. And the mind is illusion-like, empty, hollow, unreal, unconditioned. That understanding, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, of the nature of the body and of the mind — this is called <s>bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — in conventional terms, not in the ultimate sense. Why? Because <s>bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, cannot be spoken of in terms of body, mind, <s>dharma</s>, non-<s>dharma</s>, real, unreal, true, or false.

body.text: avacanīyā mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ sarvadharmaiḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ kiñcit sthānaṃ yena ca vyavahāraṃ gacchet / yathā mañjuśrīr ākāśasthānam asaṃskṛtam anutpannam aniruddham avacanīyaṃ tathā mañjuśrīr bodhir asaṃskṛtāsthānānutpannāniruddhāvacanīyā / yathā mañjuśrīr bhūtaṃ parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ sarvadharmair avacanīyam, evam eva mañjuśrīr bodhir bhūtā parigaveṣyamāṇā sarvadharmair avacanīyā / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / na mañjuśrīr bhūte vacanaṃ saṃvidyate 'nutpannāniruddhatvāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is inexpressible by all <s>dharmas</s>. Why? <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is not any place by which it could come to a conventional designation. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the station of space is unconditioned, unarisen, unceased, and inexpressible, so too, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>bodhi</s> is unconditioned, without station, unarisen, unceased, and inexpressible. Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, reality, when searched for, is inexpressible by all <s>dharmas</s>, just so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>bodhi</s>, which is reality, when searched for, is inexpressible by all <s>dharmas</s>. Why? Because, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in reality no speech is found, since it is unarisen and unceased.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr agrāhyatānālayatā / tatra mañjuśrīḥ katamāgrāhyatā katamānālayatā / cakṣuḥparijñā mañjuśrīr agrāhyatā rūpānupalabdhir anālayatā / śrotraparijñāgrāhyatā śabdānupalabdhir anālayatā / ghrāṇaparijñāgrāhyatā gandhānupalabdhir anālayatā / jihvāparijñāgrāhyatā rasānupalabdhir anālayatā / kāyaparijñāgrāhyatā spraṣṭavyānupalabdhir anālayatā / manaḥparijñāgrāhyatā dharmānupalabdhir anālayatā //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is ungraspability and non-clinging. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is ungraspability and what is non-clinging? The full comprehension of the eye, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is ungraspability; the non-apprehension of form is non-clinging. The full comprehension of the ear is ungraspability; the non-apprehension of sound is non-clinging. The full comprehension of the nose is ungraspability; the non-apprehension of odor is non-clinging. The full comprehension of the tongue is ungraspability; the non-apprehension of flavor is non-clinging. The full comprehension of the body is ungraspability; the non-apprehension of tangibles is non-clinging. The full comprehension of the mind is ungraspability; the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s> is non-clinging.

body.text: evaṃ tathāgatenāgrāhyānālayā bodhir abhisaṃbuddhā / abhisaṃbudhya cakṣuṣo 'nanugrahāya rūpānupalabdhitaś cakṣurvijñānaṃ na pratiṣṭhitam / śrotrānanugrahāya śabdānupalabdhitaḥ śrotravijñānaṃ na pratiṣṭhitam / ghrāṇānanugrahāya gandhānupalabdhito ghrāṇavijñānaṃ na pratiṣṭhitam / jihvānanugrahāya rasānupalabdhito jihvāvijñānaṃ na pratiṣṭhitam / kāyānanugrahāya spraṣṭavyānupalabdhitaḥ (

children.text: ) kāyavijñānaṃ na pratiṣṭhitam / mano'nanugrahāya dharmānupalabdhito manovijñānaṃ na pratiṣṭhitam / tenāpratiṣṭhitavijñānas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksambuddha iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati //
