Because there is no favoring of the mind, and because of the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s>, mind-consciousness is not established. Because his consciousness is thus unestablished, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, comes to be designated [as such].

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> awakened to <s>bodhi</s> as ungraspable and without clinging. And having awakened, because there is no favoring of the eye, and because of the non-apprehension of form, eye-consciousness is not established. Because there is no favoring of the ear, and because of the non-apprehension of sound, ear-consciousness is not established. Because there is no favoring of the nose, and because of the non-apprehension of odor, nose-consciousness is not established. Because there is no favoring of the tongue, and because of the non-apprehension of flavor, tongue-consciousness is not established. Because there is no favoring of the body, and because of the non-apprehension of tangibles,

body.text: catvārīmāni mañjuśrīḥ sattvānāṃ cittapratiṣṭhāni / katamāni catvāri yad uta rūpaṃ sattvānāṃ cittasya pratiṣṭhānam / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskārā mañjuśrīḥ sattvānāṃ cittasya pratiṣṭhānam / tāni khalu punar imāni mañjuśrīś catvāri cittasya pratiṣṭhānāni tathāgatenānutpannāny aniruddhānīti jñātāni //
body.translated_text: There are, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, four supports of consciousness for beings. What four? Namely, form is a support of consciousness for beings. Likewise, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, feeling, perception, and volitional formations are supports of consciousness for beings. And these four supports of consciousness, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, have been known by the <s>Tathāgata</s> to be unarisen and unceased.

body.text: bodhir iti mañjuśrīḥ śūnyatāyā etad adhivacanam / yayā śūnyatayā mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ śūnyā tayā śūnyatayā mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmāḥ śūnyāḥ / te tathāgatena yathaiva śūnyās tathaivābhisaṃbuddhāḥ / na mañjuśrīḥ śūnyatayā śūnyatābhisaṃbuddhāḥ / api tu khalu punar mañjuśrīr ekanayam etad yad uta śūnyatā vā bodhir vā / yatra mañjuśrīr na śūnyatā na bodhiḥ, na tatra mañjuśrīḥ kiṃcid dvayaṃ yena dvayena śūnyatā vā bodhir vā dvidhākriyate / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / advayā mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmā alakṣaṇā advaidhīkārā anāmāno 'nimittāś cittamanovijñānāpagatā anutpannā aniruddhā (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 61]
without conduct, without activity, without arising of conduct, beyond syllables, without sound.

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is a designation for <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). By whatever emptiness <s>bodhi</s> is empty, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, by that very emptiness all <s>dharmas</s> are empty. They have been awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> just as they are empty. Not, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, has emptiness been awakened to by emptiness. Rather, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, this is a single approach — namely, emptiness and awakening. Where, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there is neither emptiness nor awakening, there, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is no duality whatsoever by which emptiness or awakening is made twofold. Why is that? Because, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-dual, without characteristics, not made into two, without measure, without signs, gone beyond mind, mentation, and consciousness, unborn, unceased,

body.text: yat punar ucyate mañjuśrīḥ śūnyam iti, anabhiniveśagrāhasyaitad adhivacanam / na punar atra mañjuśrīḥ paramārthataḥ kaścid dharma upalabhyate yaḥ śūnyam ity ucyate / yathā mañjuśrīr ākāśam ākāśam ity ucyate, avacanīyam ākāśam / evam eva mañjuśrīḥ śūnyaṃ śūnyam ity ucyate, avacanīyeṣu śūnyeṣu praveśaḥ sarvadharmāṇām / anāmakā mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmānām ataś ca vyākriyante / na mañjuśrīr nāma deśasthaṃ na pradeśasthaṃ / tathābhisaṃbuddhās tathāgatena / nāmnā yo dharmo 'bhilapyate so 'pi dharmo na deśastho na pradeśasthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when 'empty' is said, this is a designation for the non-grasping of clinging. Not, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is there ultimately any <s>dharma</s> to be found that is called 'empty.' Just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, space is called 'space,' yet space is unspeakable — even so, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the empty is called 'empty'; it is the entry of all <s>dharmas</s> into the unspeakable emptiness. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are nameless, and yet they are declared through names. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a name does not exist in a place or in a location. Thus has the <s>Tathāgata</s> awakened. The <s>dharma</s> that is expressed by name — that <s>dharma</s> too does not exist in a place or in a location.

body.text: evam ete mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmās tathāgatena jñātā ādita evājātā anutpannā aniruddhā alakṣaṇāś cittamanovijñānāpagatā anakṣarā aghoṣāḥ / yathā jñātās tathaivādhimuktāḥ / na mañjuśrīr buddho 'dhimucyate //
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> have been known by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as originally unborn, unarisen, unceased, without characteristics, gone beyond mind, mentation, and consciousness, beyond syllables, without sound. As they have been known, so have they been resolved upon with faith. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> does not resolve upon [anything] with faith.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr ākāśasamā / ākāśaṃ ca na samaṃ na (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 62]

children.text: ) viṣamaṃ bodhir api na samā na viṣamā / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / yasya mañjuśrīr dharmasya na bhūtapariniṣpattir nāsau samo na viṣamo vā vaktavya iti / hi mañjuśrīs tathāgatena sarvadharmā asamā aviṣamā abhisaṃbuddhāḥ / tathā cābhisaṃbuddhā athāṇur api na samīkṛto na viṣamīkṛtaḥ / yādṛśā eva te dharmāḥ tādṛśā eva vijñātāḥ / bhūtajñānena katamac ca mañjuśrīḥ sarvadharmā anutpannāniruddhāḥ, abhūtvā bhavanti, abhūtvāś ca prati vigacchanti / te cāsvāmikā aparigrahāḥ saṃbhavanti, asvāmikā aparigrahāś ca mañjuśrīḥ prati vigacchanti / iti hi mañjuśrīḥ saṃbhavanti vibhavanti ca pratītya dharme vartante na cātra kaścid vartayitā / tad ucyate dharmopacchedāya tathāgato dharmaṃ deśayatīti //
children.translated_text: nor unequal; <s>bodhi</s> too is neither equal nor unequal. Why is that? Because, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>dharma</s> whose real accomplishment does not exist is not to be spoken of as either equal or unequal. For, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> have been awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as neither equal nor unequal. And having so awakened, not even an atom has been made equal or unequal. Just as those <s>dharmas</s> are, so have they been known — through knowledge of reality. And what, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>? All <s>dharmas</s> are unarisen and unceased; they come into existence without having existed, and without having existed they pass away. They arise without an owner and without possession, and without an owner and without possession, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, they pass away. Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, they arise and perish; they operate dependently, yet therein there is no one who makes them operate. Therefore it is said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of cutting off [attachment to] <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is equal to space. And space is neither equal

body.text: bodhir iti mañjuśrīr yathāvatpadam etat / tatra mañjuśrīḥ katamad yathāvatpadam / mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ, yathā bodhis tathā rūpaṃ tathatān na vyativartate / yathā bodhis tathā vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaṃ tathatān na vyativartate / yathā bodhis tathā pṛthivīdhātus tathatān na vyativartate / (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 63]

children.text: ) yathā bodhis tathāpdhātus tejodhātus tathatān na vyativartate / yathā bodhis tathā cakṣurdhātū rūpadhātuś cakṣurvijñānadhātus tathatān na vyativartate / yathā hi mañjuśrīr bodhis tathā śrotradhātuḥ śabdadhātuḥ śrotravijñānadhātuḥ, ghrāṇadhātur gandhadātur ghrāṇavijñānadhātuḥ, jihvādhātū rasadhātur jihvāvijñānadhātuḥ, kāyadhātuḥ spraṣṭavyadhātuḥ kāyavijñānadhātuḥ, manodhātur dharmadhātur manovijñānadhātus tathatān na vyativartante / etāvatī ceyaṃ dharmaprajñaptiḥ / yaduta skandhadhātvāyatanaprajñaptiḥ / sā tathāgatena yathāvadabhisaṃbuddhā yathaiva pūrvāt tathā paścāt tathā madhye / pūrvāntato 'jātāparāntato 'saṃkrāntā madhyo viviktā / evam evaiṣāṃ yathāvatpadaṃ bhavati / yathaikas tathā sarve, yathā sarve tathā caikaḥ / na cātra mañjuśrīr ekatvaṃ vā bahutvaṃ copalabhyate //
children.translated_text: As <s>bodhi</s> is, so are the water-element and the fire-element — they do not deviate from suchness. As <s>bodhi</s> is, so are the eye-element, the form-element, and the eye-consciousness element — they do not deviate from suchness. For just as, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>bodhi</s> is, so are the ear-element, the sound-element, and the ear-consciousness element; the nose-element, the odor-element, and the nose-consciousness element; the tongue-element, the taste-element, and the tongue-consciousness element; the body-element, the tangible-element, and the body-consciousness element; the mind-element, the <s>dharma</s>-element, and the mind-consciousness element — they do not deviate from suchness. And this is the full extent of the designation of <s>dharmas</s> — namely, the designation of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>). This has been awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as it really is — just as it is before, so afterward, and so in the middle. From the prior end, unborn; from the later end, not passing on; in the middle, isolated. Thus does the term 'reality as it is' apply to them. As one is, so are all; as all are, so is one. And therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, neither oneness nor multiplicity is found.

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — this is a term for 'reality as it is' (<s>yathāvatpada</s>). Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is the term for 'reality as it is'? <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>bodhi</s>: as <s>bodhi</s> is, so is form (<s>rūpa</s>) — it does not deviate from suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). As <s>bodhi</s> is, so are feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) — they do not deviate from suchness. As <s>bodhi</s> is, so is the earth-element — it does not deviate from suchness.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr ākārapraviśenānākārapraviṣṭā / tatra mañjuśrīḥ katama ākāraḥ / katamaś cānākāraḥ / ākāro mañjuśrīr ucyata ārambhaḥ sarveṣāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām / anākāra ucyate 'nupalambhaḥ sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇām / ākāra ucyate 'navasthitasya cittasyāvasthānam / anākāra ucyate (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 63]

children.text: ) 'nimittaḥ samādhir vimokṣamukham / ākāra ucyate cittanātulanāgaṇanāpratyavekṣāvimokṣaḥ sarvadharmāṇām / anākāra ucyate tulāsamatikramaḥ / katamaś ca tulāsamatikramaḥ / yatra vijñānakarma nāsti / ākāra ucyate saṃskṛtapratyavekṣā / anākāra ucyate 'saṃskṛtapratyavekṣā //
children.translated_text: the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) without signs, the gateway of liberation. Form is said to be the liberation of all <s>dharmas</s> through the non-measurement, non-counting, and non-examination of the mind. The formless is said to be the transcendence of comparison. And what is the transcendence of comparison? That in which there is no activity of consciousness. Form is said to be the examination of the conditioned. The formless is said to be the examination of the unconditioned.

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is entered into the formless through the gate of form. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is form? And what is the formless? Form, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is said to be the initiation of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. The formless is said to be the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. Form is said to be the stabilizing of the unstabilized mind. The formless is said to be

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīr anāsravo 'nupādānatā / tatra mañjuśrīḥ katamo 'nāsravaḥ katamānupādānatā / anāsravatā mañjuśrīr ucyate caturṇām āsravānāṃ vigamaḥ / katameṣāṃ caturṇām, yaduta kāmāsravasya, bhavāsravasya, avidyāsravasya, dṛṣṭvāsravasya ca, eṣāṃ caturṇām āsravāṇām / anupādānatocyate caturṇām upādānānāṃ vigamaḥ / katameṣāṃ caturṇām / kāmopādānasya, dṛṣṭyupādānasya, śīlavrataparāmarśopādānasya, ātmavādopādānasya ca, eṣāṃ caturṇām upādānānām / sarvāṇy avidyayā andhīkṛtāni, tṛṣṇayālālapitāni, anyonyābhiniveśyopādīyante / tatra mañjuśrīs tathāgata ātmavādopādānamūlaparijñātāvī / ātmaviśuddhyā sarvasattvaviśuddhim anugataḥ / yā cātmaviśuddhiḥ sā sarvasattvaviśuddhiḥ / yā sarvasattvaviśuddhir advaidhā advaidhīkārā / (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 65]
And that which is the meaning of non-duality is non-arising and non-cessation.

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) and the state of non-clinging (<s>anupādānatā</s>). Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is the undefiled, and what is non-clinging? The undefiled, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is said to be the departure of the four <s>āsravas</s> (defilements). Which four? Namely: the defilement of desire (<s>kāmāsrava</s>), the defilement of existence (<s>bhavāsrava</s>), the defilement of ignorance (<s>avidyāsrava</s>), and the defilement of views (<s>dṛṣṭvāsrava</s>) — of these four defilements. Non-clinging is said to be the departure of the four <s>upādānas</s> (attachments). Which four? The attachment of desire (<s>kāmopādāna</s>), the attachment of views (<s>dṛṣṭyupādāna</s>), the attachment of clinging to rules and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśopādāna</s>), and the attachment of the doctrine of self (<s>ātmavādopādāna</s>) — of these four attachments. All of these are blinded by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), lured by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), and are clung to through mutual fixation. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is one who has fully understood the root of attachment to the doctrine of self. Through the purification of the self, he follows the purification of all beings. And that purification of the self is the purification of all beings. That purification of all beings is non-dual, without making into two.

body.text: anutpādānirodhe mañjuśrīś cittamanovijñānaṃ na pravartate / tatra na kaścit parikalpaḥ / yena vikalpo 'yoniśo 'manasi kuryāt / sa yoniśo manaskārapravṛto 'vidyāṃ na samutthāpayati / yac cāvidyāyā asamutthānaṃ tad dvādaśānāṃ bhavāṅgānām asamutthānam / yad dvādaśānāṃ bhavāṅgānām asamutthānaṃ sājātiḥ / yā cājātiḥ sa niyāmaḥ / yo niyāmaḥ sa nītārthaḥ / yo nītārthaḥ sa paramārthaḥ / yaḥ paramārthaḥ sa niḥpudgalārthaḥ / yo niḥpudgalārthaḥ so 'nabhilāpyārthaḥ / yaś cānabhilāpyārthaḥ sa pratītyasamutpādārthaḥ / yaḥ pratītyasamutpādārthaḥ sa dharmārthaḥ / yo dharmārthaḥ sa tathāgatārthaḥ / tenocyate / yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati sa dharmaṃ paśyati / yo dharmaṃ paśyati sa tathāgataṃ paśyati / tathā ca paśyati yathā parigaveṣyamāṇo na kiṃcit paśyati / tatra mañjuśrīḥ katamat kiṃcit / yaduta cittam ārambaṇaṃ ca / sa yadā na cittam, na cārambaṇaṃ paśyati tadā bhūtam paśyati / evam ete dharmās tathāgatena saṃbuddhāḥ samatayā samāḥ //
body.translated_text: In non-arising and non-cessation, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, mind, mentation, and consciousness do not operate. Therein there is no imagining whatsoever by which one might conceptualize and attend improperly. One who is engaged in proper attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>) does not give rise to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). And the non-arising of ignorance is the non-arising of the twelve links of existence (<s>bhavāṅgas</s>). The non-arising of the twelve links of existence is non-birth (<s>ajāti</s>). Non-birth is certainty of correctness (<s>niyāma</s>). Certainty of correctness is definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>). Definitive meaning is ultimate meaning (<s>paramārtha</s>). Ultimate meaning is the meaning beyond the person (<s>niḥpudgalārtha</s>). The meaning beyond the person is the inexpressible meaning (<s>anabhilāpyārtha</s>). The inexpressible meaning is the meaning of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādārtha</s>). The meaning of dependent origination is the meaning of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmārtha</s>). The meaning of <s>Dharma</s> is the meaning of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatārtha</s>). Therefore it is said: 'One who sees dependent origination sees the <s>Dharma</s>; one who sees the <s>Dharma</s> sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' And one sees thus — when seeking, one does not see anything. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is 'anything'? Namely, mind and its object-support. When one sees neither mind nor object-support, then one sees reality. Thus have these <s>dharmas</s> been awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — equal through sameness.

body.text: bodhir mañjuśrīḥ śuddhā vimalā anaṅgaṇāḥ / tatra mañjuśrīḥ katamā śuddhiḥ, katamad vimalam, katamad anaṅgaṇam / śūnyatā mañjuśrīḥ śuddhiḥ, ānimittaṃ vimalam, (

children.translated_text: JĀA 66

children.text: ) apraṇihitam anaṅgaṇam / ajātiḥ śuddhiḥ, anabhisaṃskāro vimalam, anutpādo 'naṅgaṇam / prakṛtir viśuddhiḥ, pariśuddhir vimalam, prabhāsvaratānaṅgaṇam / aprapañcaḥ śuddhiḥ, niṣprapañco vimalam, prapañcavyupaśamo 'naṅgaṇam / tathatā viśuddhiḥ, dharmadhātur vimalam, bhūtakoṭir anaṅgaṇam / ākāśaṃ śuddhiḥ, gaganaṃ vimalam, kham anaṅgaṇam / adhyātmaḥ pariśuddhiḥ, bahirdhāpracāro vimalam, adhyātmabahirdhā cānupalabdhir anaṅgaṇam / skandhaparijñā śuddhiḥ, dhātusvabhāvo vimalam, āyatanānām apakarṣo 'naṅgaṇam / atīte kṣayajñānaṃ śuddhiḥ, anāgate 'nutpādajñānaṃ vimalam, pratyutpanne dharmadhātusthitijñānam anaṅgaṇam /
children.translated_text: <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness) is spotlessness. Non-birth is purity; non-formation is stainlessness; non-arising is spotlessness. Intrinsic purity is purity; complete purity is stainlessness; natural luminosity is spotlessness. Non-proliferation is purity; freedom from proliferation is stainlessness; the cessation of proliferation is spotlessness. <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness) is purity; <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is stainlessness; <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) is spotlessness. Space is purity; the sky is stainlessness; the void is spotlessness. Inner purity is purity; absence of outer activity is stainlessness; non-apprehension of inner and outer is spotlessness. Full understanding of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) is purity; the intrinsic nature of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) is stainlessness; the withdrawal of the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) is spotlessness. Knowledge of destruction regarding the past is purity; knowledge of non-arising regarding the future is stainlessness; knowledge of the stability of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> regarding the present is spotlessness.

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is pure, stainless, and spotless. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is purity? What is stainlessness? What is spotlessness? <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is purity; <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness) is stainlessness;

body.text: iti hi mañjuśrīḥ śuddhir vimalam anaṅgaṇam ity ekapadesmin samavasaranti / yaduta śāntapade / yac chāntaṃ tat praśāntam / yat praśāntaṃ tad upaśāntam / yad upaśāntaṃ sa upaśamaḥ / yaś copaśamaḥ sa munir ity ucyate / iti hi mañjuśrīr yathākāśaṃ tathā bodhiḥ / yathā bodhis tathā dharmāḥ / yathā dharmās tathā sattvāḥ / yathā sattvās tathā kṣetrāṇi / yathā kṣetrāṇi tathā nirvāṇam / tenocyate mañjuśrīr nirvāṇasamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / niṣṭhāparyantakāraṇe 'pratipakṣaḥ / niḥpratipakṣakāraṇenādiśuddhāḥ, ādivimalāḥ, ādyanaṅgaṇāḥ / tatra mañjuśrīs tathāgatasyaivaṃrūpān sarvadharmān abhisaṃbuddhasya sattvānāṃ (

children.translated_text: JĀA 67

children.text: ) ca dhātuṃ vyavalokayataḥ, śuddhā vimalā anaṅgaṇā vikrīḍitā nāma sattveṣu mahākaruṇāḥ pravartate //
children.translated_text: — pure, stainless, and spotless — then there arises toward beings the play called great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>).

body.translated_text: Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, purity, stainlessness, and spotlessness converge in one point — namely, in the state of peace. That which is peaceful is deeply peaceful. That which is deeply peaceful is completely pacified. That which is completely pacified is pacification. And one who has achieved pacification is called a <s>muni</s> (sage). Thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as space is, so is <s>bodhi</s>. As <s>bodhi</s> is, so are <s>dharmas</s>. As <s>dharmas</s> are, so are beings. As beings are, so are [Buddha-]fields. As fields are, so is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore it is said, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are equal to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. At the ultimate limit, there is no antidote. Because there is no antidote, [all dharmas] are primordially pure, primordially stainless, primordially spotless. Therein, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having fully awakened to all <s>dharmas</s> of such a nature, observes the disposition of beings

body.text: kathaṃ mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / yadā mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo na kṣayāya notpādāya nākṣayāya nānutpādāya nānyatkṣīṇakṣayāya ca manyate, atyantānutpādaṃ ca na vikopayati / evaṃ ca mañjuśrīś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / punar aparaṃ mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo 'tītaṃ cittaṃ kṣīṇam iti na carati / anāgataṃ cittam asaṃprāptam iti na carati / pratyutpannaṃ cittaṃ sthitam iti na carati / na cātītānāgatapratyutpanneṣu citteṣu sajati / evaṃ caran mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / dānaṃ mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ sattvāś ca tathāgataś cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram / evaṃ caran bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / śīlaṃ mañjuśrīr bodhiḥ sattvāś ca tathāgataś cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram / evaṃ caran bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / evaṃ kṣāntir bodhiḥ sattvāś ca tathāgataś ca, vīryaṃ bodhiḥ sattvāś ca tathāgataś ca, (

children.translated_text: JĀA 68

children.text: ) dhyānaṃ bodhiḥ sattvāś ca tathāgataś ca, evaṃ prajñā bodhis tathāgataś ca sattvāś cādvayam etad advaidhīkāram / evaṃ caran mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo na rūpaṃ śūnyam iti carati nāśūnyam iti / evaṃ caran mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / rūpam eva śūnyaṃ rūpasvabhāvena / evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānaṃ śūnyam iti carati nāśūnyam iti / evaṃ caran mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaś carati bodhisattvacaryāyām / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / cittamanovijñānānupalabdhitvāt / sa na kaścin mañjuśrīr dharmo vidyate, yasya parijñānaṃ vā prahāṇaṃ vā bhāvanā vā sākṣātkriyā vā bhavet / yo sā mañjuśrīr budhyate / kṣaya ity antakṣaya evāsau, yaś cātyantatatkṣīṇo na sa kṣapayitavyaḥ / akṣeyakṣīyatvād akṣayaḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / yathā ca kṣayaḥ saḥ / yaś ca yathāvat kṣayaḥ sa na kasyacit kṣayaḥ / yasya na kasyacit kṣayas tad asaṃskṛtam / yad asaṃskṛtaṃ tatra notpādo na nirodhaḥ / tenocyate / utpādād vā tathāgatānām anutpādād vā sthitaivaiṣā dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmadhātuḥ / yathā dharmadhātusthitis tathāgatajñānaṃ na pravṛttaṃ na nivṛttam / īdṛśena dharmanayapraveśena āsravā notpadyante na nirudhyante / āsravakṣaya iti mañjuśrīr vyavahārarutākṣarasaṃketaprajñaptir eṣā nātra kaścid dharma utpadyate vā nirudhyate vā //
children.translated_text: meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) is <s>bodhi</s>, and beings and the <s>Tathāgata</s> [are non-dual]; likewise, wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is <s>bodhi</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> and beings are non-dual — this is without duality. Practicing thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice thinking 'form is empty' nor 'it is not empty' — practicing thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Why is that? Because form itself is empty by its own nature. Likewise, one practices not thinking 'feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness are empty' nor 'they are not empty.' Practicing thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Why is that? Because mind, thought, and consciousness are unapprehensible. There is, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, not any <s>dharma</s> with respect to which there could be full understanding, or abandonment, or cultivation, or direct realization. That, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is what one awakens to. 'Destruction' means ultimate destruction, and that which is ultimately destroyed need not be destroyed further. Because what is beyond destruction is destroyed, it is inexhaustible. Why is that? Because destruction is as it is. That which is destruction as it is — that is not the destruction of anything. That which is not the destruction of anything — that is the unconditioned. Where there is the unconditioned, there is neither arising nor cessation. Therefore it is said: 'Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, this <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality), this stability of <s>dharma</s>, this <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), remains established.' Just as the <s>dharmadhātu</s> stability is, so <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge neither proceeds nor withdraws. Through such an entry into the method of <s>Dharma</s>, defilements (<s>āsravas</s>) neither arise nor cease. 'Destruction of defilements,' <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is merely a conventional designation in words, syllables, and signs — no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever arises or ceases therein.

body.translated_text: How, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> practice in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course? When, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not think in terms of destruction or arising, nor non-destruction or non-arising, nor otherwise-than-destroyed destruction, and does not undermine ultimate non-arising — thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, one practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> does not practice thinking 'the past mind has perished,' does not practice thinking 'the future mind has not arrived,' does not practice thinking 'the present mind is established,' nor is one attached to past, future, or present minds. Practicing thus, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Generosity (<s>dāna</s>), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is <s>bodhi</s>, and beings and the <s>Tathāgata</s> are non-dual — this is without duality. Practicing thus, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Morality (<s>śīla</s>), <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is <s>bodhi</s>, and beings and the <s>Tathāgata</s> are non-dual — this is without duality. Practicing thus, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practices in the <s>bodhisattva</s> course. Likewise, patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is <s>bodhi</s>, and beings and the <s>Tathāgata</s> [are non-dual]; vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is <s>bodhi</s>, and beings and the <s>Tathāgata</s> [are non-dual];

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya gāthābhir bhagavatam abhyaṣṭāvīt /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses:

children.translated_text: Without color, mark, or form, without cessation, without arising,
Without root, without foundation, without support — homage to you!
Without establishment, without effort, without exertion, unstable,
Freed from the six sense-bases, without support — homage to you!
Unestablished in any <s>dharma</s>, free from existence and non-existence,
Having attained the equality of formations, without support — homage to you!
Freed from the three realms, having attained the equality of space,
You are not stained by desires, without support — homage to you!

children.text: sadā samāhitaś cāsi gacchaṃs tiṣṭhaṃ śayann api /
children.translated_text: Ever in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration), whether walking, standing, or lying down,
In all modes of conduct, without support — homage to you!

children.text: samaṃ kṣeṣi samaṃ yāsi samatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: You dwell in equality, you move in equality, established in sameness,

children.text: samatāṃ na vikopesi nirālamba namo 'stu te // 6 //
children.translated_text: You do not disturb sameness, without support — homage to you!
Having entered into sameness, concentrated on all <s>dharmas</s>,
Attained to the signless attainment, without support — homage to you!
Without foundation, without support, concentrated at the summit of wisdom,
Having attained sovereignty over <s>Dharma</s>, without support — homage to you!
The forms, sounds, and conducts of all beings —
You teach in a single instant, without support — homage to you!
Freed from name and form, having cut off the cause of the aggregates,
You have entered the formless, without support — homage to you!
You have gone beyond marks, free from the making of marks,
You have entered the signless, without support — homage to you!
Of unconstructed intention, with unestablished mind,
Beyond mindfulness and mental engagement, without support — homage to you!
Without attachment like space, beyond proliferation, unstained,
Your mind is equal to space, without support — homage to you!
Infinite and without middle is space, and such is the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature) of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
Having transcended the three times, without support — homage to you!
The <s>Buddhas</s> have the characteristics of space, and space too is without characteristics,
Freed from cause and effect, without support — homage to you!
Ungraspable like the moon in water, unsupported in any <s>dharma</s>,
Without ego, without sound, without support — homage to you!
You are unsupported in the aggregates, in the elements, and in the sense-bases,
Freed from perversion, without support — homage to you!
Freed from both extremes, having cut off the view of self,
Having attained the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, without support — homage to you!
Freed from the enumeration of forms, free from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>,
Without grasping, without abandonment, without support — homage to you!
Having transcended the faults of <s>Māra</s>, having reached the <s>dharmadhātu</s> as destination,
You are one whose <s>dharma</s> is unobstructed, without support — homage to you!

children.text: astīti nocyate 'rthajñaiḥ nāstīty api tu nocyate /
children.translated_text: 'It exists' is not said by those who know meaning; 'it does not exist' is also not said;
Beyond the path of speech, without grasping, without support — homage to you! // 21 //
Not relying on the <s>dharma</s> of duality, you have cut down the banner of pride;
Liberated from both duality and non-duality, without support — homage to you! // 22 //

children.text: jitās te mānasā doṣāḥ śārīrāś ca caturvidhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Conquered are your mental faults and the fourfold bodily [faults];
Inconceivable, beyond comparison, without support — homage to you! // 23 //
You operate without deliberate effort, free from all faults;
Your activity is preceded by knowledge, without support — homage to you! // 24 //

children.text: anāsravā te smṛtiḥ sūkṣmā bhūtābhūteṣu tanmayā /
children.translated_text: Your mindfulness is without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), subtle, immersed in things real and unreal;
Without abode, without intention, without support — homage to you! // 25 //
With a mind that has no object, you comprehend all minds;

children.text: na cātmaparasaṃjñā te nirālamba namo 'stu te // 26 //
children.translated_text: Yet you have no notion of self and other, without support — homage to you! // 26 //
Without object, without support, not deluding any mind,
You are of the nature of objectlessness, without support — homage to you! // 27 //

children.text: anārambaṇaṃ ca taccittaṃ svabhāvena na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And that objectless mind does not exist by its own nature;
Inconceivable, having attained sameness (<s>samatā</s>), without support — homage to you! // 28 //
With unsupported knowledge you see all <s>Buddha-fields</s> (<s>kṣetra</s>),
And the conduct of all beings, without support — homage to you! // 29 //

children.text: cittaṃ na labdhaṃ buddhehi atyantāya kadācana /
children.translated_text: The mind has never been found by the <s>Buddhas</s> for all eternity;

children.text: sarvadharmā ca sarvajña nirālamba namo 'stu te // 30 //
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> too, O Omniscient One (<s>Sarvajña</s>), without support — homage to you! // 30 //

children.text: māyopamāḥ sarvadharmā māyā caiva na vidyate /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are like a magical illusion (<s>māyā</s>), and the illusion itself does not exist;
Liberated from the nature of illusion, without support — homage to you! // 31 //
You move in the world, O Awakened One (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>), not relying on worldly <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: lokaṃ na ca vikalpeṣi nirālamba namo 'stu te // 32 //
children.translated_text: And you do not conceptualize the world, without support — homage to you! // 32 //
You move in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) due to emptiness, with emptiness as your domain;

children.text: śūnyaṃ ca śūnyam ākhyāsi nirālamba namo 'stu te // 33 //
children.translated_text: And you declare emptiness to be empty, without support — homage to you! // 33 //
You perform transformations with great supernatural power, through illusion-like <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption);
Having attained the state beyond diversity, without support — homage to you! // 34 //
Neither one nor many, you do not dwell in far or near;
Without casting up, without casting down, without support — homage to you! // 35 //
Awakened in a single moment through the <s>vajra</s>-like <s>samādhi</s> (diamond-like absorption);
Having attained the state beyond appearance, without support — homage to you! // 36 //
You know <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as unmoving, O leader in all three times;
Endowed with various skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), without support — homage to you! // 37 //
Skilled in the knowledge of means for beings through successive [guidance],

children.text: acalaṃ vetsi nirvāṇaṃ nirālamba namo 'stu te // 38 //
children.translated_text: You know <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as unmoving, without support — homage to you! // 38 //
Without sign (<s>nimitta</s>), without deliberate effort (<s>ābhoga</s>), without conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), without affliction,
Without appearance, without self, one — without support, homage to you! // 39 //
Free from conceptual construction, without self-possession, just as you [know] yourself by yourself,

children.text: vetsi sarvajña sarvatra nirālamba namo 'stu te // 40 //
children.translated_text: You know, O Omniscient One, everywhere, without support — homage to you! // 40 //

children.text: vandāmi tvāṃ daśabala oghatīrṇaṃ vandāmi tvāṃ abhayadadaṃ viśāradam /
children.translated_text: I pay homage to you, O Ten-Powered One (<s>Daśabala</s>), who has crossed the flood; I pay homage to you, the giver of fearlessness, the confident one;

children.text: dharmeṣu āveṇikaniścayaṃ gataṃ vandāmi tvāṃ sarvajagasya nāyakam // 1 //
children.translated_text: Gone to certainty regarding the exclusive (<s>āveṇika</s>) <s>dharmas</s> — I pay homage to you, the leader of the entire world. // 1 //

children.text: vandāmi saṃyojanabandhanacchidaṃ vandāmi tvāṃ pāragataṃ sthule sthitam /
children.translated_text: I pay homage to the cutter of the bonds of fetters; I pay homage to you, gone beyond, established in the gross;

children.text: vandāmi tvāṃ khinnajagasya nāyakaṃ vandāmi saṃsāragata-ṃ-aniśritam // 2 //
children.translated_text: I pay homage to you, the leader of the weary world; I pay homage to one gone into <s>saṃsāra</s> yet not relying [upon it]. // 2 //
I pay homage to one gone beyond the settling of beings in all destinies, whose mind is liberated in all births;

children.text: jale ruhaṃ vā salilair na lipyase niṣevitā te munir buddha śūnyatā // 3 //
children.translated_text: Like a lotus in water, you are not stained by the waters — O Sage (<s>Muni</s>), O <s>Buddha</s>, you have cultivated emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). // 3 //

children.text: vivekatā śāstṛpadaṃ niruttaraṃ vande nirālamba mahaughatīrṇam /
children.translated_text: Seclusion (<s>viveka</s>) is the unsurpassed station of the Teacher — I pay homage to the supportless one who has crossed the great flood;

children.text: vibhāvitā sarvanimitta sarvaśo na te kahiṃcit praṇidhānu vidyate // 4 //
children.translated_text: All signs are illuminated in every way by you — yet nowhere is any resolve of yours to be found. // 4 //

children.text: acintiyaṃ buddha mahānubhāvaṃ vandāmi ākāśasamam aniśritam /
children.translated_text: Inconceivable, O <s>Buddha</s>, is your great power — I pay homage to the one equal to space, without reliance;

children.text: vandāmi te sarvaguṇāgradhāri vandāmi tvāṃ merum ivodgataśriyam // 5 //
children.translated_text: I pay homage to you, bearer of the highest of all virtues; I pay homage to you, whose glory rises like Mount <s>Meru</s>. // 5 //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya sādhukāram adāt / sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ / subhāṣitaṃ te mañjuśrīr evam eva / mañjuśrīr na buddhā rūpato draṣṭavyā na dharmato na lakṣaṇato na dharmadhātutaḥ / na buddhā ekākino na mahājanamadhyagatāḥ / na buddhā kenacid dṛṣṭāḥ, na śrutā na pūjitā na pūjyante / na buddhā kasyacid dharmasya ekatvaṃ vā bahutvaṃ vā kurvanti / na buddhair bodhiḥ prāptā / na buddhāḥ kenacid dharmena prabhāvyante / na buddhaiḥ kaścid dharmo dṛṣṭo na śruto na smṛto na vijñāto nājñātaḥ / na buddhair bhāṣitaṃ nodāhṛtam, na buddhā bhāṣanti nodāharanti, na buddhā bhāṣiṣyanti nodāhariṣyanti / na buddhā abhisaṃbudhyanti, na buddhaiḥ kaścid dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddhaḥ / na buddhānāṃ kleśāḥ prahīṇāḥ, na vyavadānaṃ sākṣātkṛtam / na buddhaiḥ kaścid dharmo dṛṣṭaḥ, na śruto nāghrāto na vijñātaḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ / ādipariśuddhatvāt sarvadharmāṇām //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) gave his approval to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! Your words are well spoken, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> — just so, just so. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s> are not to be seen through form, nor through <s>dharma</s>, nor through marks, nor through the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). The <s>Buddhas</s> are neither solitary nor among the multitude. The <s>Buddhas</s> have not been seen by anyone, nor heard, nor worshiped, nor are they being worshiped. The <s>Buddhas</s> do not make any <s>dharma</s> one or many. <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) has not been attained by the <s>Buddhas</s>. The <s>Buddhas</s> are not illuminated by any <s>dharma</s>. No <s>dharma</s> has been seen, heard, remembered, cognized, or known by the <s>Buddhas</s>. The <s>Buddhas</s> have not spoken nor set forth [the <s>Dharma</s>]; the <s>Buddhas</s> do not speak nor set forth; the <s>Buddhas</s> will not speak nor set forth. The <s>Buddhas</s> do not attain complete awakening; no <s>dharma</s> has been awakened to by the <s>Buddhas</s>. The defilements of the <s>Buddhas</s> have not been abandoned; purification has not been directly realized. No <s>dharma</s> has been seen, heard, smelled, or cognized by the <s>Buddhas</s>. Why is that? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are primordially pure.'

body.text: V
body.translated_text: V

body.text: (1) yaḥ kaścin mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamān sattvān pratyekajinatve sthāpayed idaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ nādhimuktaḥ / yo cānyo mañjuśrīr bodhisattva imaṃ dharmaparyāyam adhimucyet / ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati /
body.translated_text: (1) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, some <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish beings equal in number to the atoms of dust of the trichiliocosm in the state of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Buddha), yet did not have faith in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — and another <s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were to have faith in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — this one would produce far greater merit.

body.text: kaḥ punar vādo ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhed lekhāpayed vā / ayam eva tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: What need to mention one who would write this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse or cause it to be written? This very one would produce far greater merit.

body.text: (2) yāvanto mañjuśrīr bodhisattva trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāḥ saṃvidyante, aṇḍajā vā, jarāyujā vā, saṃsvedajā vā, opapādukā vā, rūpiṇo vā, arūpiṇo vā, saṃjñino vā, asaṃjñino vā, apadā vā, dvipadā vā, catuḥpadā vā, bahupadā vā, sarve te parikalpam upādāya, apūrvācaramaṃ mānuṣyakam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilabheyuḥ / mānuṣyakam ātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhya bodhicittam utpādayeyuḥ / bodhicittam utpādya ekaiko bodhisattvo gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ buddhakṣetraparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ saśrāvakāṇāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upatiṣṭhet / sarvasukhopadhānāni copasaṃharet / gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyāṃ kalpāṃs (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 79]

children.text: ) teṣāṃ ca parinirvṛtānāṃ stūpāni kārayet, ratnamayāni, yojanaśatocchritāni, ratnavedikāparivṛtāni, maṇimuktāratnadāmakṛtaśobhāni, ucchritacchatradhvajapatākāni, vaśirājamaṇiratnajālasaṃcchannāni /
children.translated_text: and were to build <s>stūpas</s> for those who have passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> — <s>stūpas</s> made of jewels, rising a hundred <s>yojanas</s> high, encircled by jeweled railings, adorned with garlands of gems, pearls, and jewels, with raised parasols, banners, and pennants, covered with nets of <s>vaśirāja-maṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems;

body.translated_text: (2) <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, as many beings as exist in the trichiliocosm — born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, or born spontaneously, with form or formless, with perception or without perception, without feet, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed — if all of them, by way of supposition, were to obtain a human body for the first and only time, and having obtained a human body were to generate the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), and having generated the thought of awakening, each <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to attend upon <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and their <s>Śrāvaka</s>-communities equal in number to the atoms of dust of innumerable <s>Buddha-fields</s> as [countless as] the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicine for the sick — and were to provide all comforts, for <s>kalpas</s> (eons) as innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

body.text: yo cānyo bodhisattva āśayasaṃpannaḥ / imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāraṃ śrutvādhimucyed avataret pattīyet paribuddhet / antaśa ekām api gāthām uddiśed ayaṃ tato saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet / buddhajñānānugamanaṃ saṃvartakam asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya / asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya sa pūrvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu śatatamām api kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamām api, koṭīśatasahasratamām api, kalām api, gaṇanām api, upamām api, upaniṣadam api nopaiti //
body.translated_text: yet another <s>Bodhisattva</s>, endowed with [proper] intention, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — the 'Ornament of the Light of Knowledge Entering the Domain of All <s>Buddhas</s>' (<s>Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatāra-jñānālokālaṃkāra</s>) — were to have faith in it, enter into it, trust in it, and comprehend it, or were to recite even a single verse from it — this one would produce immeasurably greater merit. This merit-formation leads to the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. Compared to this merit-formation, that former merit-formation — the gift-based meritorious activity of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — does not approach even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth-of-a-<s>koṭi</s> part, nor any fraction, calculation, comparison, or analogy.

body.text: (1) yaḥ kaścin mañjuśrīr gṛhī bodhisattvo gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyān buddhān bodhisattvān saśrāvakasaṃghān gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyān (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 80]

children.text: ) kalpān cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upatiṣṭhet / yaś cānyaḥ pravrajito bodhisattvaḥ śīlavān āśayasaṃpanno 'ntaśo yas tiryagyonigate 'pi sattva ekasyāpy ālopaṃ dadyāt / tasya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya pūrvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamām api kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamām api, koṭīśatasahasratamām api, koṭīniyutasahasratamām api, yāvad upaniṣadam api na kṣamate //
children.translated_text: ...for [many] <s>kalpas</s> with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick. And if another renunciant <s>Bodhisattva</s>, virtuous and endowed with pure intention, were to give even a single morsel of food to even a being born in the animal realm — the former mass of merit would not reach even a hundredth part of the merit-formation of this one, nor a thousandth,

body.translated_text: (1) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, some householder <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to [attend upon] <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, together with their <s>Śrāvaka-saṃghas</s>, innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

body.text: (2) sacen mañjuśrīs trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvāḥ pravrajitāḥ śīlavanta āśayaśuddhāḥ, tata ekaiko bodhisattvo gaṅgānadīsikatāsaṃkhyeyān buddhān bodhisattvān saśrāvakasaṃghāṃś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariskārair upatiṣṭhet, gaṅgānadīsikatāsaṃkhyeyān kalpān / yas teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāro bhaved dānamayaḥ / yo vānyo bodhisattva āśayaśuddho śīlavān gṛhī vā pravrajito vā, imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvādhimucyet pattīyed vā likheta lekhāpayed vā / asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya sa pūrvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu śatatamīm api kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamīm api, yāvad upaniṣām api na kṣamate //
body.translated_text: (2) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of dust in a great trichiliocosm were renunciants, virtuous, and pure in intention, and each one of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were to attend upon <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and their <s>Śrāvaka</s> assemblies equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick, for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>...

body.text: (3) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo mahāsattvas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ saptaratnaparipūrṇāṃ kṛtvā buddhebhyo bhagavadbhyo dānaṃ dadyāt / evaṃ dadan trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān dānaṃ dadyāt / yo vānyo bodhisattva imān dharmaparyāyān antaśaś catuṣpādikāṃ gāthāṃ bodhisattvasya deśayet / asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya sa pūrvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamām api kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamām api, śatasahasratamām api, koṭīśatasahasratamām api, yāvad upaniṣām api na kṣamate //
body.translated_text: (3) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> were to fill the great trichiliocosm with the seven precious things and give a gift to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and giving thus, were to give gifts for <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of dust in the trichiliocosm — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to recite from this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse even a single verse of four lines for the purpose of awakening...

body.text: (4) tiṣṭhantu tāvan mañjuśrīḥ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamān kalpān dānaṃ dadataḥ puṇyābhisaṃskārāḥ / sacen mañjuśrīr gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyā bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ / tata ekaiko bodhisattvo gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jāmbūnadasuvarṇamayāni, sarvavṛkṣāṃś ca divyair vastraiḥ pariveṣṭayitvā, sarvaprabhāsamuccayamaṇiratnajālasaṃcchannāni kṛtvā, vaśirājamaṇiratnamayaiḥ kūṭāgārair vidyutpradīpamaṇiratnavedikāparivṛtaiḥ paripūrṇāṃ kṛtvā, ucchritacchatradhvajapatākābhir gaṅgānadīsikatāsaṃkhyeyebhyo buddhebhyo divase divase dānaṃ dadyāt / evaṃ dadaṅ gaṅgāsikatāsaṃkhyeyān kalpān dānaṃ dadyāt / yo vānyo bodhisattva imaṃ dharmaparyāyam adhimucyānyasya bodhisattvasyeto dharmaparyāyād antaśa ekām api catuṣpādikāṃ gāthāṃ deśayed avatārayed (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 82]

children.text: ) vā / asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya sa pūrvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāras teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānamayaḥ śatatamām api kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamām api, śatasahasratamām api, saṃkhyām api, kalām api, gaṇanām api, upaniṣām api, yāvad upaniṣadam api nopaiti //
children.translated_text: ...the former mass of merit of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, consisting of giving, would not reach even a hundredth part of the merit-formation of this one, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor any calculation, portion, fraction, or comparison — it would not reach even a comparison.

body.translated_text: (4) Set aside, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the merit-formations of giving gifts for <s>kalpas</s> equal to the atoms of the trichiliocosm. If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there were <s>Bodhisattvas</s> innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and each one of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were to make <s>Buddha</s>-fields innumerable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> entirely of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, and adorn all trees with divine garments...

body.text: (1) tadyathā mañjuśrīs traidhātukaparyāpannāḥ sarvasattvā narakatiryakpretayamalokopapannā bhaveyuḥ / atha gṛhī bodhisattvas tān sarvān narakatiryakpretayamalokād uddhṛtya pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattvaḥ pravrajito 'ntaśas tiryagyonigate 'pi sattva ekam ālopaṃ dadyāt / ayaṃ tato bahutaram asaṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavayāt //
body.translated_text: (1) Suppose, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all beings belonging to the triple world were born in the hells, animal realm, <s>Preta</s>-realm, and <s>Yama</s>-world. Then a lay <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to rescue them all from the hells, animal realm, <s>Preta</s>-realm, and <s>Yama</s>-world and establish them in <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-hood. Yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a renunciant, were to give even a single morsel of food to even a being born in the animal realm — this one...

body.text: (2) sacen mañjuśrīr daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ pravrajitā bodhisattvā bhaveyuḥ / tata ekaiko bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣv ekaikasmin digbhāge daśabuddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamān buddhān bhagavataḥ paśyet / ekaikaṃ ca tathāgataṃ sabodhisattvaṃ saśrāvakaṃ daśasu buddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamaṇurajaḥsamān (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 83]

children.text: ) kalpāṃś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upatiṣṭhet / ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya divase divase buddhakṣetrānabhilāpyakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparamāṇurajaḥsamān lokadhātūn vaśirājamaṇiratnapratipūrṇān kṛtvā dānaṃ dadyāt / yo vānyo bodhisattvo 'smin dharmaparyāye 'dhimukto 'ntaśas tiryagyonigate 'pi sattva ekam ālopaṃ dadyāt / asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya pūrvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāras teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dānamayaḥ śatatamām api kalāṃ nopaiti, sahasratamām api, śatasahasratāmām api, saṃkhyām api, kalām api, gaṇanām api, upaniṣām api, upaniṣadam api na kṣamate / tat kasya hetoḥ / avaivartikānāṃ bodhisattvānām iyaṃ mudrā yadutāsya dharmaparyāyasya śravaḥ //
children.translated_text: ...for [many] <s>kalpas</s> were to attend [them] with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick; and to each <s>Tathāgata</s>, day after day, were to make world-realms equal in number to the atoms of indescribable <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields entirely filled with <s>vaśirāja</s> jewels and give them as gifts — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having faith in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, were to [even briefly embrace it]...

body.translated_text: (2) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in the ten directions there were renunciant <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the atoms of indescribable <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and each one of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were to see in each direction in each region <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, equal in number to the atoms of ten indescribable <s>koṭī</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, and each <s>Tathāgata</s>...

body.text: (1) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sattvān śraddhānusāritve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvam arthānusāritve pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: (1) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in the following of faith (<s>śraddhānusāritva</s>) — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in the following of meaning (<s>arthānusāritva</s>) — this one generates immeasurably more merit.

body.text: (2) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśadikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān arthānusāritve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvaṃ dharmānusāritve pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 84]
generates immeasurably more merit.

body.translated_text: (2) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in the following of meaning — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in the following of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānusāritva</s>) — this one

body.text: (3) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sattvān dharmānusāritve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvaṃ srotāpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: (3) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in the following of the <s>Dharma</s> — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpatti</s>) — this one generates immeasurably more merit.

body.text: (4) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān srota-āpattiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: (4) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in the fruit of stream-entry — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>) — this one generates immeasurably more merit.

body.text: (5) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān sakṛdāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvam ānāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: (5) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in the fruit of once-returning — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>) — this one generates immeasurably more merit.

body.text: (6) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān anāgāmiphale pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo (

children.translated_text: [JĀA 85]

children.text: ) vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvaṃ arhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in <s>Arhat</s>-ship — this one generates immeasurably more merit.

body.translated_text: (6) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in the fruit of non-returning — yet if another

body.text: (7) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān arhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvaṃ pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavati //
body.translated_text: (7) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in <s>Arhat</s>-ship — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-hood — this one generates immeasurably more merit.

body.text: (8) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān pratyekabuddhatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvaṃ bodhicitte pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato 'saṃkhyeyataraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: (8) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-realms in the ten directions in <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-hood — yet if another <s>Bodhisattva</s> were to establish even a single being in the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) — this one would generate immeasurably more merit.

body.text: (9) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasattvān bodhicitte pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva ekaṃ sattvam avaivartikatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: (9) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in all world-systems in the ten directions in the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) — yet another <s>bodhisattva</s> who establishes even a single being in the state of non-retrogression (<s>avaivartika</s>) would produce far greater merit than that.

body.text: (10) sacen mañjuśrīr bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattvān avaivartikatve pratiṣṭhāpayet / yo vānyo bodhisattva imaṃ dharmaparyāyam adhimuktaḥ likhāpayitvā parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayet, antaśa ekaṃ sattvam apy asmin dharmaparyāye 'vatārayet / ayaṃ tato bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet //
body.translated_text: (10) If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to establish all beings in the state of non-retrogression — yet another <s>bodhisattva</s> who, having faith in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, has it written down and reveals it in detail to others, introducing even a single being into this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — this one would produce far greater merit than that.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyām imā gāthā abhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: yo bodhisattvo daśabuddhakoṭināṃ saddharmaṃ dhārayet kṣayāntakāle /
children.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> who upholds the true <s>Dharma</s> of ten <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> at the end of the age —

children.text: sūtraṃ ca yo 'nyaḥ śṛṇuyāt sagauravād idaṃ tataḥ puṇyamahāntaṃ viśeṣayet // 1 //
children.translated_text: Yet another who would hear this <s>sūtra</s> with reverence would surpass even that great merit. // 1 //

children.text: yo buddhakoṭīdaśa pūjayed ṛddhyā samākramya daśāsu dikṣu /
children.translated_text: One who, having risen by supernatural power, would worship ten <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions,

children.text: vandāpayet sa puruṣāṃś ca sarvān kṛtvā kṛpāṃ sarvasukheṣv agṛddhaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: And who would cause all people to pay homage, being compassionate and unattached to all pleasures — // 2 //

children.text: yaś cedaṃ sūtraṃ jinadharmasūcakaṃ parasya deśeta muhūrtakaṃ pi /
children.translated_text: Yet if one were to teach this <s>sūtra</s> that points to the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) to another, even for a moment,

children.text: prasannacittaḥ sugatasya śāsana idaṃ tataḥ puṇyaphalaṃ viśiṣyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: With a serene mind, in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) — the fruit of merit of this surpasses that. // 3 //
Having shown the <s>sūtra</s> proclaimed by the <s>Sugata</s>, which is a lamp for gods and humans,

children.text: sa tīkṣṇaprajñaś ca mahābalaś ca buddhāna bhūmiṃ labhate ca śīghram // 4 //
children.translated_text: One of sharp wisdom and great power quickly attains the stage of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // 4 //

children.text: kathāṃ śruṇitvā sugatānam īdṛśaṃ saṃśrāvayed yaś ca dvitīyasattve /
children.translated_text: Having heard such a discourse of the <s>Sugatas</s>, one who would cause a second being to hear it,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca buddhāna narottamānāṃ parinirvṛtānāṃ nirupādhiśeṣe // 5 //
children.translated_text: And of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme among men, who have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without remainder — // 5 //
Establish lofty and beautiful <s>stūpas</s>, adorned with excellent jewels reaching up to the summit of existence,

children.text: chatraiḥ patākais tatha ghaṇṭaśabdaiḥ pariṇāhavante hi yathā bhavāgram // 6 //
children.translated_text: With parasols, banners, and the sound of bells, as extensive as the peak of existence. // 6 //

children.text: icche tv ayaṃ kaścid iha bodhisattvaḥ sūtraṃ śruṇitvā ima evarūpam /
children.translated_text: Should any <s>bodhisattva</s> here, having heard this <s>sūtra</s> of such a nature, desire —

children.text: kāye pratiṣṭhāpayi pustake vā idaṃ tataḥ puṇyaphalaṃ viśiṣyate // 7 //
children.translated_text: To establish it upon the body or in a book — the fruit of merit of this surpasses that. // 7 //

children.text: yo bodhisattvo imu dharmu dhārayed apanītamāccharyamalo viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> who would uphold this <s>Dharma</s>, free from wonder, with defilements removed, confident,

children.text: puṇyaṃ bhavet tasya hi aprameyaṃ labheta bodhiṃ ca yathepsitena // 8 //
children.translated_text: The merit of that one would indeed be immeasurable, and one would attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) as desired. // 8 //

children.text: idaṃ hi sūtraṃ sugataiḥ praśastaṃ parigṛhītaṃ bahubodhisattvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> is praised by the <s>Sugatas</s>, embraced by many <s>bodhisattvas</s>;

children.text: tathāgatānām iha-m-ātmabhāva ākāśadhātve hi sarveṣu darśitaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: The self-nature of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is herein revealed in all the realms of space. // 9 //

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanā āryamañjuśrīr bodhisattvaḥ, te ca daśadiganantāparyantāśeṣalokadhātusaṃnipatitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā iti ca mahāśrāvakāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti // //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, was delighted, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who had assembled from the boundless, infinite, and exhaustless world-systems in the ten directions, and the great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> — all rejoiced at the words spoken by the Blessed One.

body.text: āryasarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam // //
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Sūtra</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> called '<s>Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra</s>' (The Ornament of the Light of Wisdom that Enters the Domain of All <s>Buddhas</s>) is completed.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> that arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: And that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic.

body.text: deyadharmo 'yaṃ pravaramahāyānayāyinaḥ bhikṣuśīladhvajasya ca tatra puṇyaṃ tad bhavatv ācāryopādhyāyamātāpitṛpūrvaṃgamaṃ kṛtvā sakalasattvarāśer anuttarajñānaphalāvāptaya iti //
body.translated_text: This is the meritorious gift of the monk <s>Śīladhvaja</s>, one who follows the excellent <s>Mahāyāna</s>. May that merit, with teachers, preceptors, mother and father placed foremost, be for the attainment of the fruit of supreme knowledge by the entire multitude of beings.

body.text: mahārājādhirājaśrīmadgopāladevarājye saṃvat 12 śrāvaṇadine 30 likhitam idaṃ upasthāyakacāṇḍokeneti // śrī //
body.translated_text: This was written in the reign of the great king of kings, the glorious <s>Gopāladeva</s>, in the year 12, on the 30th day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, by the attendant <s>Cāṇḍoka</s>. Auspiciousness!
